questions.stem: A 32-year-old man has a 1-week history of diarrhea, bloating, and excessive gas. He describes his stools as very foul-smelling, greasy, and floating. The week before symptoms began he went on a camping trip, slept outside, and drank unfiltered stream water. He is otherwise healthy. Microscopic examination of the stool shows rapidly motile single-celled organisms that have two nuclei and flagella. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Balantidium coli

choices.label: B
choices.text: Giardia lamblia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Leishmania spp.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trypanosome spp.

explanation.summary: Greasy, foul-smelling stools after drinking untreated surface water, with binucleate flagellated protozoa in stool, indicate giardiasis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Giardia lamblia is a flagellate protozoan whose organisms show two nuclei and flagella, exactly as described on stool microscopy. G. lamblia survives in the environment for months, so campers and people who drink unfiltered outdoor water are at risk in addition to person-to-person fecal-oral spread. Beyond generic gastrointestinal symptoms, giardiasis characteristically produces smelly, greasy, fatty stools.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Balantidium coli is a ciliate whose surface is covered by cilia rather than a few flagella, and it has no binucleate appearance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Leishmania spp. are flagellates, but they are not acquired by drinking contaminated water and do not produce fatty stools.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Naegleria fowleri is an amoeba that moves by pseudopods and causes a brain infection, not watery greasy diarrhea.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trypanosome spp. are flagellates that are not transmitted in stream water and are not diagnosed by stool microscopy.

questions.stem: In everyday usage, a parasite is any organism that lives on or inside a host and takes nutrients from it. In medicine, however, the word is applied much more narrowly. Which of the following descriptions matches the medical definition of a parasite?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A eukaryotic fungus that invades and damages host tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: A eukaryotic organism that infects humans and is not a fungus

choices.label: C
choices.text: A prokaryotic organism that colonizes the host intestine

choices.label: D
choices.text: An agent that is neither prokaryotic nor eukaryotic in structure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Any organism that takes nutrients from the host it lives on

explanation.summary: Medically, a parasite is a eukaryotic organism that infects humans but is not a fungus.
explanation.whyCorrect: The medical definition deliberately excludes bacteria, viruses, and fungi. Bacteria are prokaryotic and therefore not classified as parasites, and viruses are neither prokaryotic nor eukaryotic, so they also fall outside the category. What remains are eukaryotic, non-fungal organisms such as protozoa and helminths.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fungi are eukaryotic but are specifically excluded by the medical definition of a parasite.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bacteria are prokaryotic, so they are excluded from the medical definition even though they take nutrients from the host.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This describes viruses, which are neither prokaryotic nor eukaryotic and therefore fall outside the medical category.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This is the broad, general definition, under which most pathogens would qualify as parasites.

questions.stem: Parasites are broken down into two broad categories, ectoparasites and endoparasites. Which of the following features defines an ectoparasite?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It interacts only superficially and does not invade deeper tissues

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is always multicellular, whereas endoparasites are single-celled

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is prokaryotic, whereas endoparasites are eukaryotic organisms

choices.label: D
choices.text: It provides a nutritional benefit to the host it colonizes

choices.label: E
choices.text: It requires an arthropod vector, whereas endoparasites are ingested

explanation.summary: An ectoparasite interacts only superficially with its host and does not invade deeper tissues.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ectoparasites such as mosquitoes, ticks, fleas, lice, bedbugs, and mites live on the surface of the host. Endoparasites, by contrast, infect beyond the skin and advance into the organ systems. The superficial versus deep distinction, not size or cell type, is what separates the two groups.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Both groups contain multicellular members; helminths are multicellular endoparasites, so this does not separate them.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neither group is prokaryotic; parasites by the medical definition are eukaryotic organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Parasitism is a one-sided relationship in which the host receives no benefit.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ectoparasites can be vectors themselves rather than requiring one, and endoparasites are acquired by many routes.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man presents with an intensely itchy rash on his hands, feet, and waistline that is worst at night and disturbs his sleep. Physical examination shows small erythematous papules and burrow-like tracks between the fingers. He has been staying in a crowded shelter since losing his home to a natural disaster. Which of the following is the most likely etiologic agent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diphyllobothrium latum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Necator spp.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Plasmodium vivax

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sarcoptes scabiei

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wuchereria bancrofti

explanation.summary: An intensely itchy papular rash with burrows between the fingers, acquired in crowded living conditions, is scabies.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sarcoptes scabiei is a microscopic mite that burrows into the skin and is transmitted through close personal contact or shared fomites, which makes crowded settings such as shelters, jails, childcare facilities, and nursing homes high risk. The lesions are small papules, burrows, and excoriations that favor the finger webs, skin folds, waistline, genitals, nipples, and buttocks. Itching is characteristically worse at night.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Diphyllobothrium latum is the fish tapeworm and causes gastrointestinal symptoms after eating undercooked fish.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Necator spp. are nematodes that penetrate the skin of bare feet and then infect the gastrointestinal tract.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Plasmodium vivax causes malaria with cyclic fever and chills and is spread by the Anopheles mosquito.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Wuchereria bancrofti is transmitted by mosquito bites and causes lymphatic filariasis with massive limb swelling, not burrows.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman has a scabies infestation with an intensely pruritic papular rash. The mites in her skin release soluble antigens in their saliva, eggs, feces, and other secretions. Which of the following best describes the immune reaction these antigens provoke and the cell chiefly responsible for the resulting tissue injury?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct complement activation, with the alternative pathway lysing host epidermal cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Type I hypersensitivity, begun by IgE and mast cells and then dominated by eosinophils

choices.label: C
choices.text: Type II hypersensitivity, with IgG binding antigens on host keratinocyte surfaces

choices.label: D
choices.text: Type III hypersensitivity, with immune complexes depositing in dermal blood vessels

choices.label: E
choices.text: Type IV hypersensitivity, with sensitized T cells recruiting and activating macrophages

explanation.summary: Scabies antigens trigger a Type I hypersensitivity reaction that is quickly taken over by eosinophils, which cause the tissue damage.
explanation.whyCorrect: Soluble mite antigens produce a Type I hypersensitivity reaction initiated by IgE and mast cells. That initial reaction is rapidly dominated by eosinophils, which release the factors ultimately responsible for tissue injury. This mechanism explains why the rash is so intensely itchy and inflamed relative to the small number of mites present.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Complement-mediated lysis of host epidermal cells is not the pathway described for scabies.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Antibody directed against antigens fixed on host cell surfaces is not how the mite antigens act here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immune complex deposition in vessel walls is not the described mechanism of scabies skin injury.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The reaction is not a delayed, T cell and macrophage driven process; it begins with IgE and mast cells.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old nursing home resident has an itchy papular rash with excoriations over the trunk and hands, and the physician suspects scabies. Which of the following is the most appropriate test to confirm the diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Colonoscopy with inspection of the bowel for attached worms

choices.label: B
choices.text: Giemsa-stained thick blood smear examined for larval worms

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lumbar puncture with microscopic examination of spinal fluid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Skin scraping examined microscopically for mites, eggs, or feces

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stool examination for cysts and flagellated organisms

explanation.summary: Scabies is confirmed by scraping the skin and identifying the mite, its eggs, or its feces under the microscope.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because Sarcoptes scabiei lives in burrows within the superficial skin, scraping the involved skin samples the organism directly. The scraping is examined under the microscope for the mite itself, its eggs, or its feces. No blood, stool, or spinal fluid testing is needed for this superficial ectoparasite.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Colonoscopy detects intestinal helminths and would not sample a mite living in the skin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A Giemsa-stained thick blood smear is used to look for bloodborne worm larvae, such as in lymphatic filariasis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Spinal fluid examination is used when a brain infection such as primary amebic meningoencephalitis is suspected.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Stool examination for cysts and flagellated organisms is how giardiasis is diagnosed.

questions.stem: A 4-month-old infant is brought to clinic with an intensely itchy rash, and skin scraping confirms Sarcoptes scabiei. Compared with the usual pattern in healthy adults, which of the following distributions is most characteristic of scabies in infants and immunocompromised patients?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Finger webs, wrists, and waistline only

choices.label: B
choices.text: Genitals, nipples, and buttocks only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Groin and axillae, with sparing of the hands

choices.label: D
choices.text: Head, face, neck, palms, and soles

choices.label: E
choices.text: Lower legs at the site of larval entry

explanation.summary: Infants and immunocompromised patients with scabies may develop rash on the head, face, neck, palms, and soles.
explanation.whyCorrect: Scabies lesions can appear anywhere on the body, but in healthy adults they are most commonly found between the fingers, in skin folds, along the waistline, and on the genitals, nipples, or buttocks. Infants and immunocompromised patients extend beyond that adult pattern and may have rash on the head, face, neck, palms, and soles. Recognizing this broader distribution prevents a missed diagnosis in these groups.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Finger webs, wrists, and waistline describe the classic adult pattern, which is the comparison group in this question.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Genitals, nipples, and buttocks are also typical adult sites rather than the distinguishing infant pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Scabies characteristically involves the hands, so a pattern sparing them does not fit this infestation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lesions at a larval entry site on the legs describe skin-penetrating nematodes, not a burrowing mite.

questions.stem: A patient with an intensely itchy rash that is worse at night has thin, winding, snake-like lines in the skin of the finger webs in addition to small papules and excoriations. Which of the following best explains these linear lesions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Excoriations created entirely by the patient's own scratching

choices.label: B
choices.text: Linear pustules that follow the course of cutaneous nerves

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serpiginous burrows made as the mite tunnels through the skin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vesicles formed by mast cell degranulation around dermal vessels

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wheals caused by adult worms moving through subcutaneous fat

explanation.summary: The snake-like lines of scabies are burrows tunneled by the mite and are described as a serpiginous rash.
explanation.whyCorrect: Scabies mites burrow into the skin, and the resulting tunnels can be seen on the surface as lines that look like snakes. These are called serpiginous rashes and are a hallmark of the infestation. They occur alongside the small papules and excoriations, and the associated itching is characteristically worse at night.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Scratching produces excoriations, but the winding tracks are made by the mite itself as it burrows.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The burrows follow the mite's path through the skin, not the distribution of cutaneous nerves.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Although mast cells participate in the hypersensitivity response, the visible lines are tunnels, not vesicles around vessels.
whyWrongByChoice.E: No adult worm migrates through subcutaneous fat in scabies; the organism is a microscopic mite in the skin.

questions.stem: Over 6 weeks, several residents of a nursing home develop intensely itchy rashes with burrows, and two staff members become affected as well. Which of the following best explains how the responsible organism spread through this facility?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bites from mosquitoes breeding in standing water nearby

choices.label: B
choices.text: Close personal contact and sharing of contaminated fomites

choices.label: C
choices.text: Drinking tap water that contains environmental cyst forms

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ingestion of food contaminated with parasite eggs and feces

choices.label: E
choices.text: Walking barefoot on soil that contains infective larvae

explanation.summary: Scabies spreads by close personal contact and shared fomites, which is why outbreaks cluster in crowded institutions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Transmission of Sarcoptes scabiei occurs through close personal contact or shared fomites such as bedding and clothing. That is why outbreaks are common in childcare facilities, jails, and nursing homes, where people are in sustained close contact and share items. Staff who handle residents and their linens are exposed by the same route.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mosquito bites transmit organisms such as Plasmodium spp. and Wuchereria bancrofti, not a skin-burrowing mite.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Contaminated drinking water transmits protozoa such as Giardia lamblia rather than an ectoparasitic mite.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fecal-oral ingestion transmits organisms such as Giardia lamblia and Ascaris spp., not scabies.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Soil contact with bare feet transmits skin-penetrating nematodes such as Strongyloides, Ancylostoma, and Necator spp.

questions.stem: A lecturer states that, after humans, mosquitoes are the most lethal animal on earth, even though an individual mosquito bite causes only a small local reaction. Which of the following best explains this statement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mosquito bites cause fatal anaphylaxis in most exposed people

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mosquito saliva contains a toxin that is lethal in large doses

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mosquitoes act as vectors for parasites, bacteria, and viruses

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mosquitoes invade deep tissue and destroy the lymphatic system

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mosquitoes reproduce within human skin and cause chronic rashes

explanation.summary: Ectoparasites such as mosquitoes are dangerous mainly because they transmit other pathogens, not because of the bite itself.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ectoparasites in and of themselves are largely an inconvenience, but their role as vectors for other parasites and microorganisms is deadly. Mosquitoes carry parasites, bacteria, and viruses, and the infections they spread cause millions of deaths worldwide every year. Malaria alone, transmitted by the Anopheles mosquito, is the most lethal parasitic infection on earth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Most bites cause only a minor local reaction rather than fatal systemic allergy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The danger comes from organisms the mosquito carries, not from a toxin in its saliva.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The mosquito is a superficial ectoparasite; it is the worm it can transmit that damages the lymphatic system.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mosquitoes do not reproduce inside human skin; that behavior belongs to mites such as Sarcoptes scabiei.

questions.stem: Endoparasites are further broken down into two subcategories. Which of the following correctly distinguishes those two groups?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Protozoa are always motile, whereas helminths are never motile

choices.label: B
choices.text: Protozoa are multicellular, whereas helminths are single-celled

choices.label: C
choices.text: Protozoa are prokaryotic, whereas helminths are eukaryotic

choices.label: D
choices.text: Protozoa are single-celled, whereas helminths are multicellular

choices.label: E
choices.text: Protozoa infect only skin, whereas helminths infect organ systems

explanation.summary: Endoparasites are subdivided by cellularity: protozoa are single-celled and helminths are multicellular worms.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both groups are endoparasites, meaning they infect beyond the skin and advance into the organ systems. Protozoa are single-celled endoparasites, while helminths, the worms, are multicellular endoparasites. This size difference is practical as well: protozoa require a microscope, whereas helminths can be enormous, with the fish tapeworm reaching over 30 feet.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Motility does not separate the groups; some protozoa are non-motile in parts of their life cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This reverses the definitions; protozoa are the single-celled group.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neither group is prokaryotic, since parasites by the medical definition are eukaryotes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Infection limited to the skin surface describes ectoparasites, not either subcategory of endoparasite.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man has several days of diarrhea with blood and mucus after fecal-oral exposure on a farm. Stool microscopy shows a large single-celled organism whose entire outer edge appears fuzzy because it is covered with thousands of tiny hair-like projections. Which of the following is the most likely organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Balantidium coli

choices.label: B
choices.text: Giardia lamblia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: D
choices.text: Plasmodium vivax

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trypanosome spp.

explanation.summary: Balantidium coli is the only ciliate known to infect humans and can cause gastroenteritis with diarrhea or dysentery.
explanation.whyCorrect: Parasites that move by cilia are rare causes of human disease, and B. coli is the only known ciliate that infects humans. Its fuzzy outer edge on microscopy is created by thousands of tiny cilia. B. coli is transmitted fecal-orally and usually causes asymptomatic infection, but in rare cases it produces gastroenteritis with accompanying diarrhea or dysentery.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Giardia lamblia is a flagellate with two nuclei and a few whip-like flagella, not a surface covered in cilia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Naegleria fowleri is an amoeba that moves by pseudopods and causes a brain infection rather than dysentery.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Plasmodium vivax is a sporozoan transmitted by mosquitoes and causes malaria, not bloody diarrhea.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trypanosome spp. are flagellates and are not identified in stool as large ciliated organisms.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old boy develops fever, headache, neck stiffness, and confusion 5 days after repeatedly diving into a warm freshwater lake in August. He is started on antibiotics for presumed bacterial meningitis. Examination of the cerebrospinal fluid shows motile single-celled organisms that move by extending blunt projections of cytoplasm. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Balantidium coli

choices.label: B
choices.text: Giardia lamblia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: D
choices.text: Schistosoma mansoni

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wuchereria bancrofti

explanation.summary: Meningitis-like illness after diving in warm fresh water, with amoebas in spinal fluid, indicates Naegleria fowleri.
explanation.whyCorrect: Naegleria fowleri is an amoeba that moves by pseudopods, the blunt cytoplasmic projections seen in the spinal fluid. It is found in warm fresh water and causes primary amebic meningoencephalitis, which presents much like meningitis and is frequently misdiagnosed as bacterial meningitis at first. Infections typically follow swimming or diving in a lake or river during the summer months.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Balantidium coli is a ciliate acquired fecal-orally that causes intestinal disease, not central nervous system infection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Giardia lamblia is a flagellate that causes diarrhea and is not found in cerebrospinal fluid.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Schistosoma mansoni is a blood fluke whose adults live in mesenteric veins after freshwater skin penetration.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Wuchereria bancrofti is a mosquito-borne nematode that lodges in the lymphatic system, not the brain.

questions.stem: A previously healthy teenager develops primary amebic meningoencephalitis after warm lake water was forced up his nose while he was diving. Which of the following describes how the organism reached his brain?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Along the olfactory nerve and through the cribriform plate

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct extension from the middle ear through the mastoid

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hematogenous seeding from a skin entry site on the foot

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lymphatic spread from cervical nodes into the meninges

choices.label: E
choices.text: Retrograde spread along the optic nerve from the orbit

explanation.summary: Naegleria fowleri travels from the nose up the olfactory nerve and enters the brain through the cribriform plate.
explanation.whyCorrect: When warm water shoots up the nose, the parasite gains access to the olfactory nerve, which is cranial nerve I. It travels along that nerve and enters the brain through the cribriform plate. This anatomic route explains why nasal exposure, rather than swallowing the water, is the risk factor for this infection.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Spread from the middle ear is not the described mechanism for this amoeba.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Skin penetration at the foot is the route used by nematodes such as Strongyloides, Ancylostoma, and Necator spp.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lymphatic spread characterizes lymphatic filariasis, not primary amebic meningoencephalitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The organism uses the olfactory nerve, cranial nerve I, not the optic nerve.

questions.stem: The family of a patient with primary amebic meningoencephalitis caused by Naegleria fowleri asks about the likelihood of survival. Which of the following best characterizes the mortality of this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: About 10 percent of patients die

choices.label: B
choices.text: About 25 percent of patients die

choices.label: C
choices.text: About 50 percent of patients die

choices.label: D
choices.text: About 75 percent of patients die

choices.label: E
choices.text: About 98 percent of patients die

explanation.summary: Naegleria fowleri infection is nearly always fatal, with roughly 98 percent mortality.
explanation.whyCorrect: Between 1962 and 2023, 164 cases of N. fowleri infection were reported and only 4 people survived. That record gives the amoeba a roughly 98 percent mortality, making it one of the most lethal infections known. Its rarity is the only reason it does not contribute more deaths than far more common parasites.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A 10 percent death rate vastly understates an infection in which only 4 of 164 reported patients survived.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A 25 percent death rate would imply most patients recover, which is the opposite of the reported experience.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Survival is far worse than a coin flip for this infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Even 75 percent understates the mortality, which approaches nearly every reported case.

questions.stem: A single-celled endoparasite is observed in the laboratory moving by pushing a blunt projection of its cytoplasm outward and then flowing into it. Which of the following categories of protozoa does this organism belong to?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoebas

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ciliates

choices.label: C
choices.text: Flagellates

choices.label: D
choices.text: Helminths

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sporozoans

explanation.summary: Protozoa that move using pseudopods, blunt cytoplasmic projections, are classified as amoebas.
explanation.whyCorrect: Some protozoa move by pushing a projection of cytoplasm outward, a structure called a pseudopod, which literally means false foot. Protozoa that use pseudopods to move are called amoebas. An infamous example is Naegleria fowleri, the brain-eating amoeba.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ciliates move using a bunch of small, hair-like cilia rather than cytoplasmic projections.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Flagellates move using whip-like flagella, as Giardia lamblia does.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Helminths are multicellular worms, not single-celled protozoa.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sporozoans are defined by complicated life cycles rather than by a single mode of movement.

questions.stem: Some protozoa have extremely complicated life cycles and can be either motile or non-motile depending on the phase of life they are in, so they do not fit into the categories defined by a single mode of movement. Which of the following categories includes these organisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoebas

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cestodes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ciliates

choices.label: D
choices.text: Flagellates

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sporozoans

explanation.summary: Sporozoans are the protozoa with complicated life cycles that include both motile and non-motile phases.
explanation.whyCorrect: The four broad categories of protozoa are amoebas, flagellates, ciliates, and sporozoans. The first three are defined by how the organism moves, using pseudopods, flagella, or cilia respectively. Sporozoans are the exception: their life cycles are complicated, sometimes with both motile and non-motile phases, and Plasmodium spp. are an example.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoebas are defined by consistent movement using pseudopods.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cestodes are tapeworms, which are multicellular helminths rather than protozoa.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ciliates are defined by movement using cilia, and Balantidium coli is the only human-infecting example.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Flagellates are defined by movement using whip-like flagella.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old traveler returns from sub-Saharan Africa with cyclic fevers, chills, and fatigue and is diagnosed with malaria. Which of the following transmitted the causal organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Eating undercooked freshwater fish

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fecal-oral ingestion of contaminated water

choices.label: C
choices.text: Larvae penetrating the skin of a bare foot

choices.label: D
choices.text: Skin contact with freshwater cercariae

choices.label: E
choices.text: The bite of an Anopheles mosquito

explanation.summary: Plasmodium spp., the cause of malaria, are transmitted by the Anopheles mosquito.
explanation.whyCorrect: Plasmodium spp. are sporozoan protozoa transmitted by the bite of the Anopheles mosquito. Malaria is the most lethal parasitic infection on earth. Because transmission depends on the mosquito, control efforts center on reducing mosquito populations, using insect repellent and bed nets, and improving access to anti-malaria drugs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Eating undercooked fish transmits Diphyllobothrium latum, the fish tapeworm.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fecal-oral ingestion transmits protozoa such as Giardia lamblia and Balantidium coli.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Larvae penetrating bare feet is the route used by Strongyloides, Ancylostoma, and Necator spp.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Freshwater cercariae released from snails cause schistosomiasis after penetrating skin.

questions.stem: A patient with uncomplicated malaria describes a flu-like illness in which fever and chills come and go rather than persisting. Which of the following best describes the typical pattern in most patients?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Continuous high fever without any remission for two weeks

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fever and chills that fluctuate every two to three days

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fever only in the evenings, resolving fully by the morning

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fever starting six months after exposure and lasting years

choices.label: E
choices.text: One febrile episode followed by lifelong protective immunity

explanation.summary: Most patients with malaria have flu-like fever and chills that fluctuate on a two to three day cycle.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most patients with malaria experience flu-like symptoms with fever and chills that fluctuate every 2 to 3 days, and then recover. The cyclic pattern reflects the complicated life cycle of these sporozoan parasites. Although most patients recover, malaria can be lethal in vulnerable populations, particularly young children.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Unremitting fever for two weeks does not match the cyclic pattern described for malaria.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A strictly evening fever pattern is not the described cycle of malarial fever and chills.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Onset delayed six months with years of continuous fever does not describe the usual course.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A single episode with lifelong immunity is not how malaria behaves; recurring febrile cycles are typical.

questions.stem: A global health resident is asked to summarize the burden of malaria for the year 2022. Which of the following sets of figures is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: About 1 billion cases and 5 million deaths, mostly older adults

choices.label: B
choices.text: About 3 million cases and 600 deaths, mostly in North America

choices.label: C
choices.text: About 25 million cases and 60,000 deaths, mostly in Europe

choices.label: D
choices.text: About 50 million cases and 2 million deaths, evenly distributed

choices.label: E
choices.text: About 249 million cases and 608,000 deaths, mostly African children

explanation.summary: In 2022 there were an estimated 249 million malaria cases and 608,000 deaths, most of them children in sub-Saharan Africa.
explanation.whyCorrect: Globally, an estimated 249 million cases of malaria occurred in 2022, with 608,000 deaths. Most of those deaths were children in sub-Saharan Africa. Control efforts have been very successful, cutting malaria mortality by 36 percent globally from 2010 to 2020, but significant challenges remain.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A billion cases and five million deaths overstate the burden, and older adults are not the group most affected.
whyWrongByChoice.B: These numbers are orders of magnitude too small for a disease that kills hundreds of thousands yearly.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Both figures are far too low, and Europe is not where the burden of malaria falls.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Malaria deaths are heavily concentrated in sub-Saharan Africa rather than evenly distributed worldwide.

questions.stem: A 3-year-old child in a daycare has 10 days of greasy, foul-smelling diarrhea, and giardiasis is suspected. Which of the following findings in a stool specimen would establish the diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoebas moving by broad cytoplasmic pseudopods

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ciliated organisms with a fuzzy outer border

choices.label: C
choices.text: Flagellated organisms or cyst forms of the parasite

choices.label: D
choices.text: Segmented worm fragments containing a uterus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Worm larvae identified on a Giemsa-stained smear

explanation.summary: Giardiasis is diagnosed by examining stool for the flagellated or cyst form of the parasite.
explanation.whyCorrect: Examination of the stool for the flagellated or cyst form of the parasite is how giardiasis is diagnosed. The flagellated form is recognizable by its two nuclei and its whip-like flagella, and it moves rapidly on a fresh specimen. The cyst form is what allows G. lamblia to survive in the environment for months and spread in water.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoebas moving by pseudopods are not the form found in giardiasis, which is caused by a flagellate.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ciliated organisms with a fuzzy border would indicate Balantidium coli, the only ciliate that infects humans.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Segmented worm fragments with a uterus are proglottids shed by a tapeworm, not a protozoan.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Worm larvae on a Giemsa-stained blood smear point to lymphatic filariasis from Wuchereria bancrofti.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man is diagnosed with giardiasis after drinking unfiltered stream water on a camping trip. He is counseled to avoid drinking unfiltered water in the future. Which of the following is the appropriate drug therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Albendazole

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chloroquine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ivermectin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Metronidazole

choices.label: E
choices.text: Praziquantel

explanation.summary: Giardiasis is treated with metronidazole, an anti-parasitic drug, along with counseling to avoid unfiltered water.
explanation.whyCorrect: A patient with foul-smelling, greasy diarrhea and flagellated binucleate protozoa in the stool has giardiasis. Management pairs prevention counseling, chiefly avoiding drinking unfiltered water, with metronidazole, an anti-parasitic drug. Because G. lamblia also spreads person-to-person fecal-orally, hygiene matters as well.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Albendazole is not the agent used here for a flagellate protozoan infection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chloroquine is an anti-malarial agent and does not treat giardiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ivermectin is not the drug identified for treatment of giardiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Praziquantel is not the anti-parasitic used to treat giardiasis in this patient.

questions.stem: A public health nurse investigates a cluster of giardiasis among toddlers at a daycare center. None of the children have been camping and all drink treated municipal water. Which of the following best explains the spread of Giardia lamblia in this setting?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Airborne droplets released when infected children cough

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bites from arthropod vectors living in the play area

choices.label: C
choices.text: Larvae in the sandbox soil penetrating bare feet

choices.label: D
choices.text: Person-to-person fecal-oral spread in a crowded setting

choices.label: E
choices.text: Undercooked fish served in the daycare cafeteria

explanation.summary: Giardia lamblia spreads person-to-person fecal-orally and moves rapidly through densely populated settings such as daycares.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although contaminated outdoor water and pools are classic sources, G. lamblia is spread person-to-person fecal-orally as well. It spreads rapidly in densely populated areas like daycares, where hand hygiene and diapering make fecal-oral transfer easy. Outbreaks therefore occur without any outdoor water exposure at all.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Giardiasis is not a respiratory infection and is not transmitted by airborne droplets.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Arthropod vectors transmit organisms such as Plasmodium spp. and Wuchereria bancrofti, not Giardia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Skin penetration by soil larvae is how Strongyloides, Ancylostoma, and Necator spp. infect a host.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Undercooked fish transmits Diphyllobothrium latum, a tapeworm, not a flagellate protozoan.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man who frequently prepares homemade sushi has several months of fatigue, mild abdominal discomfort, and weight loss. Laboratory studies show vitamin B12 deficiency, and during a routine colonoscopy a very long segmented worm is discovered. Which of the following is the most likely organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ascaris spp.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Diphyllobothrium latum

choices.label: C
choices.text: Necator spp.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Schistosoma japonicum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Taenia solium

explanation.summary: A very long segmented intestinal worm with vitamin B12 deficiency after eating raw fish is the fish tapeworm.
explanation.whyCorrect: Diphyllobothrium latum, the fish tapeworm, is one of the largest helminths and can grow to over 30 feet inside the human intestine. It is contracted by eating undercooked fish. Most cases are asymptomatic, but some patients develop abdominal discomfort, weight loss, and vitamin B12 deficiency, and many infections are discovered incidentally during routine colonoscopy or when dislodged worms pass in the stool.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ascaris spp. are round, non-segmented nematodes transmitted fecal-orally rather than by eating fish.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Necator spp. are nematodes that penetrate the skin of bare feet before reaching the gastrointestinal tract.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Schistosoma japonicum is a blood fluke acquired through freshwater skin contact, and adults live in veins.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Taenia solium is the pork tapeworm and is not the species associated with vitamin B12 deficiency from raw fish.

questions.stem: A patient treated for fish tapeworm infection asks how to keep from becoming infected again. Which of the following measures is most effective?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Avoiding skin contact with warm freshwater lakes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cooking or freezing fish before it is served

choices.label: C
choices.text: Filtering all drinking water before it is consumed

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sleeping under an insecticide-treated bed net

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wearing shoes when walking outdoors on soil

explanation.summary: Cooking or freezing fish before serving destroys the larval stage of Diphyllobothrium latum and prevents infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Diphyllobothrium latum is contracted by eating undercooked fish, so the prevention step targets the larval stage found in fish. Cooking the fish or freezing it prior to serving destroys that larval stage. No water filtration, footwear, or vector control is needed for this particular parasite.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Avoiding warm fresh water reduces risk of Naegleria fowleri and schistosome cercariae, not fish tapeworm.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Filtering drinking water prevents waterborne protozoa such as Giardia lamblia, not a fish-borne tapeworm.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bed nets prevent mosquito-borne infections such as malaria and lymphatic filariasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Footwear prevents skin penetration by nematodes such as Strongyloides, Ancylostoma, and Necator spp.

questions.stem: A worm recovered from a patient's stool is round in cross-section, has no segments along its body, possesses both a mouth and an anus, and belongs to a species in which males and females are separate individuals. Which of the following categories does this worm belong to?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cestodes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ciliates

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nematodes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Protozoa

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trematodes

explanation.summary: A round, non-segmented worm with a complete digestive tract and separate sexes is a nematode.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nematodes, or roundworms, are named after the shape of their bodies: round and non-segmented, similar in appearance to earthworms. They have a complete digestive system with both a mouth and an anus, which distinguishes them from cestodes. They also have separate sexes, unlike some other helminths that are hermaphroditic.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cestodes are flat and highly segmented and lack a complete digestive tract.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ciliates are a category of single-celled protozoa, not multicellular worms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Protozoa are single-celled organisms and have no mouth, anus, or sexes in this sense.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trematodes are flat and leaf-shaped with no segmentation, and most are hermaphroditic.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old child living in an area with poor sanitation is found to be infected with Ascaris spp. Which of the following is the usual route of transmission for this nematode?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Contact with cercariae in fresh water

choices.label: B
choices.text: Eating undercooked freshwater fish

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fecal-oral ingestion of the parasite

choices.label: D
choices.text: Larval penetration of intact skin

choices.label: E
choices.text: The bite of an infected mosquito

explanation.summary: Ascaris spp. are nematodes transmitted by the fecal-oral route.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nematodes have multiple ways to infect hosts depending on the species. Some are transmitted fecal-orally, and Ascaris spp. are the example of that route. Other nematodes burrow through skin or are delivered by insect bites, so knowing the species determines the exposure history to ask about.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cercariae in fresh water are the infective larval form of Schistosoma spp., which are trematodes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Eating undercooked fish transmits Diphyllobothrium latum, which is a cestode rather than a nematode.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Skin penetration is the route used by Strongyloides, Ancylostoma, and Necator spp.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mosquito bites transmit Wuchereria bancrofti among the nematodes.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man who spent a month walking barefoot in a rural tropical village develops raised, red, serpent-like lines on the top of one foot. Several weeks later he develops abdominal pain and diarrhea. Which of the following best explains this sequence of findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A fluke larva released by snails entering skin and reaching the liver

choices.label: B
choices.text: A mite tunneling within the outer layers of the foot skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: A mosquito-borne worm obstructing lymphatic drainage of the leg

choices.label: D
choices.text: A tapeworm scolex anchoring into the wall of the small intestine

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nematode larvae penetrating the skin and then infecting the gut

explanation.summary: Serpent-like skin lines at a bare-foot entry site followed by gastrointestinal illness indicate skin-penetrating nematodes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Strongyloides, Ancylostoma, and Necator spp. can all penetrate healthy human skin and then infect the gastrointestinal tract, which is why infection is common in people who walk barefoot in endemic areas. As the larvae search for a blood vessel under the skin, inflammation produces serpent-like lines near the entry site, a finding called cutaneous larva migrans. The later abdominal symptoms reflect the worms arriving in the gut.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Schistosome cercariae come from freshwater contact and their adults settle in veins, not the gut lumen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A burrowing mite causes intensely itchy lesions concentrated in finger webs and skin folds, not later gut infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A mosquito-borne worm lodging in lymphatics causes massive limb swelling rather than skin tracks and diarrhea.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A tapeworm is acquired by ingestion and produces no migrating skin tracks at a foot entry site.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man living in a tropical region develops progressive, massive swelling of both legs over several years. A thick blood smear stained with Giemsa shows slender worm larvae. Which of the following best explains his condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diphyllobothrium latum attached in the small intestine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri entering through the cribriform plate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sarcoptes scabiei burrowing in the skin of both legs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Schistosoma mansoni adults living in mesenteric veins

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wuchereria bancrofti adults living in the lymphatic system

explanation.summary: Massive leg swelling with worm larvae on a blood smear is lymphatic filariasis caused by Wuchereria bancrofti.
explanation.whyCorrect: W. bancrofti is a nematode transmitted by the bites of mosquitoes, after which it migrates to the lymphatic system. The inflammation caused by adult worms there leads to tissue damage and an inability to drain fluid from the extremities. In severe cases massive fluid accumulation occurs, usually in the legs, producing the disease called lymphatic filariasis or elephantiasis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The fish tapeworm causes abdominal discomfort, weight loss, or vitamin B12 deficiency, not leg swelling.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Naegleria fowleri causes a rapidly fatal brain infection after warm fresh water enters the nose.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Scabies causes an intensely itchy papular rash with burrows, not massive chronic limb swelling.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Schistosoma mansoni adults in mesenteric veins produce gastrointestinal disease from trapped eggs.

questions.stem: Helminths are divided into three categories. Which of the following lists those three categories correctly?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoebas, flagellates, and ciliates

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nematodes, cestodes, and trematodes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Protozoa, sporozoans, and helminths

choices.label: D
choices.text: Roundworms, flukes, and flagellates

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tapeworms, mites, and blood flukes

explanation.summary: The three categories of helminths are nematodes, cestodes, and trematodes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nematodes are also known as roundworms, cestodes are also known as tapeworms, and trematodes are also known as flukes. All three are multicellular endoparasites, which distinguishes them from the single-celled protozoa. Their body plans differ: round and non-segmented, flat and segmented, and flat and leaf-shaped respectively.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoebas, flagellates, and ciliates are categories of protozoa, not helminths.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Protozoa and sporozoans are single-celled groups, and helminths is the parent category itself.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Flagellates are protozoa, so this list mixes a protozoan category with two helminth groups.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mites are ectoparasites, and blood flukes are a subset of trematodes rather than a separate category.

questions.stem: A long worm passed by a patient is flat, looks like a strand of tape, and is made of many repeating units. Which of the following describes the basic body plan of this organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A flat, leaf-shaped body with no segmentation at all

choices.label: B
choices.text: A male and a female worm joined within a body groove

choices.label: C
choices.text: A round, unsegmented body with a mouth and an anus

choices.label: D
choices.text: A scolex, an unsegmented neck, and segmented proglottids

choices.label: E
choices.text: A single cell with a fuzzy border of short cilia

explanation.summary: Cestodes have three main parts: a scolex, an unsegmented neck, and a highly segmented body of proglottids.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cestodes are called tapeworms because they appear like long strands of tape and have flat, segmented bodies. They have three main parts: a scolex, which is the head, an unsegmented neck, and a highly segmented body. The individual segments of that body are called proglottids.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A flat, leaf-shaped body without segmentation describes a trematode, or fluke.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Paired male and female worms joined in a body groove describe adult Schistosoma spp.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A round, unsegmented body with a complete digestive tract describes a nematode.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A single cell with a fuzzy ciliated border describes a ciliate protozoan such as Balantidium coli.

questions.stem: The head of a pork tapeworm, Taenia solium, is examined under the microscope. Which of the following structures allows this organism to anchor itself to the host gastrointestinal wall?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A gynaecophoral canal that clamps onto the mucosa

choices.label: B
choices.text: A muscular pharynx that grips the mucosal surface

choices.label: C
choices.text: A series of suckers and a rostellum bearing hooks

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cutting plates that shear into intestinal epithelium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sticky secretions released from terminal proglottids

explanation.summary: Taenia solium anchors to the gut wall using a series of suckers and a hooked rostellum on its scolex.
explanation.whyCorrect: The scolex, or head, of a cestode contains appendages that allow the worm to anchor into the gastrointestinal wall, and these vary from species to species. Taenia solium, the pork tapeworm, has a series of suckers and a rostellum with hooks on its head. This attachment matters clinically, because an intact head and neck can keep generating new segments.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The gynaecophoral canal is a body groove of adult male schistosomes used to hold the female during mating.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cestodes lack a complete digestive tract and have no muscular pharynx for feeding or attachment.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cutting plates are not the attachment structure described for the pork tapeworm scolex.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Proglottids are the reproductive segments at the far end of the worm and are shed, not used to attach.

questions.stem: Unlike a roundworm, a tapeworm recovered from the human intestine has neither a mouth nor an intestinal tract of its own. Which of the following explains how a cestode obtains nutrients from its host?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It absorbs nutrients from the host across its body surface

choices.label: B
choices.text: It digests host tissue with enzymes released from its scolex

choices.label: C
choices.text: It feeds on host blood drawn in through the genital pore

choices.label: D
choices.text: It gathers nutrients using cilia that sweep along its body

choices.label: E
choices.text: It ingests host cells through a specialized oral sucker

explanation.summary: Cestodes lack a complete digestive tract and absorb nutrients from the host directly through their body surface.
explanation.whyCorrect: Unlike nematodes, which have a complete digestive system with both a mouth and an anus, cestodes do not have a complete digestive tract. They absorb nutrients from their host through their body surface instead. Their flat, highly segmented shape maximizes the surface available for that absorption.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The scolex is an attachment organ with suckers and sometimes hooks, not a digestive structure.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The genital pore is part of the reproductive apparatus of a proglottid and is not used for feeding.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cilia are a feature of ciliate protozoa such as Balantidium coli, not of tapeworms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cestodes have no oral sucker for ingesting host cells, since they have no mouth at all.

questions.stem: A patient treated for a tapeworm infection passes a chain of segments in the stool and feels better. Several months later, segments appear in the stool again even though he has not traveled or changed his diet. Which of the following best explains the recurrence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Eggs in the bowel hatched directly into new adult worms

choices.label: B
choices.text: Shed proglottids regrew a new scolex and neck in the bowel

choices.label: C
choices.text: The head and neck were undamaged and made new proglottids

choices.label: D
choices.text: The passed proglottids reinfected him through the anal canal

choices.label: E
choices.text: The worm migrated out of the gut into deeper host tissue

explanation.summary: If the scolex and neck of a tapeworm survive, the worm keeps producing new proglottids and eggs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Loss of proglottids is a normal part of the worm's life cycle, and passing a chain of segments is often how patients learn they are infected. If the head and neck of the worm are undamaged, it can continue to make more and more proglottids and eggs. Recurrent segments in the stool therefore suggest the scolex was never eliminated.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Eggs do not hatch directly into adult worms within the bowel; consumption of eggs or proglottids spreads the worm.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Proglottids are terminal reproductive segments and do not regenerate a scolex and neck.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Shed proglottids are passed out of the body, and spread occurs when eggs or proglottids are consumed.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Although some cestodes can penetrate deeper tissue, that would not explain new segments appearing in stool.

questions.stem: Trematodes are flat, leaf-shaped worms with no segmentation, and most of them are hermaphroditic. Schistosoma spp. are a notable exception to that rule. Which of the following describes adult Schistosoma worms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Flat, segmented worms whose distal segments each contain eggs

choices.label: B
choices.text: Leaf-shaped worms bearing both suckers and a hooked rostellum

choices.label: C
choices.text: Round, unsegmented worms with a complete digestive tract

choices.label: D
choices.text: Separate males and females, the female held in a body groove

choices.label: E
choices.text: Single hermaphroditic worms that self-fertilize within the liver

explanation.summary: Schistosoma spp. are the trematode exception: they have separate sexes, and the male holds the female in a gynaecophoral canal.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most flukes are hermaphroditic, but Schistosoma spp. have male and female sexes. Adult male schistosomes possess a body groove called a gynaecophoral canal, and during mating the female sits inside this canal. The paired worms then migrate together to veins around the bladder and to the mesenteric vein for sexual reproduction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Flat, segmented worms with egg-bearing distal segments describe cestodes and their proglottids.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Suckers and a hooked rostellum describe the scolex of Taenia solium, a tapeworm.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Round, unsegmented worms with a complete digestive tract describe nematodes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Schistosoma spp. are precisely the trematodes that are not hermaphroditic.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man who waded in a freshwater river in a tropical region several months ago now has painless hematuria and intermittent abdominal pain. Parasite eggs are found in both his urine and his stool. Which of the following best describes how this infection developed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adult worms attached to bladder mucosa using suckers and hooks

choices.label: B
choices.text: Amoebas entered the nose and spread through the cribriform plate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cercariae from snails penetrated skin and adults reached pelvic veins

choices.label: D
choices.text: Larvae were swallowed in river water and matured inside the stomach

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mosquitoes injected larvae that then migrated into lymphatic vessels

explanation.summary: Schistosomiasis follows skin penetration by cercariae from freshwater snails, with adults settling in veins around the bladder and bowel.
explanation.whyCorrect: Schistosomiasis, also called snail fever, is caused by S. haematobium, S. mansoni, and S. japonicum, which infect freshwater snails as part of the life cycle. The larval cercariae are released from snails into fresh water and penetrate the skin of humans on contact. The immature parasite migrates to the liver, and after maturation the male and female worms move to veins around the bladder and to the mesenteric vein, so eggs are shed in both urine and stool.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Suckers and hooks are attachment structures of a tapeworm scolex, not of a blood fluke in a vein.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nasal entry and passage through the cribriform plate describe Naegleria fowleri infection of the brain.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Infection begins with skin penetration by cercariae in fresh water, not by swallowing larvae.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mosquito-borne larvae migrating to lymphatics describe Wuchereria bancrofti and lymphatic filariasis.

questions.stem: A 14-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department with a severe frontal headache, fever, and vomiting that began 5 days after he spent an afternoon diving into a warm freshwater lake. Over the next day he develops a stiff neck and has a generalized seizure. A wet preparation of his cerebrospinal fluid shows motile amebae. Which of the following routes of entry best explains how this organism reached his brain?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct extension from a middle ear infection through the mastoid air cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Entry through the nasal mucosa with spread along the olfactory nerve

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hematogenous seeding of the meninges from an unrecognized lung infection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ingestion of lake water with absorption of the organism across the intestinal wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inoculation of the organism through a small abrasion on the skin of his leg

explanation.summary: Naegleria fowleri infects when contaminated water is forced up the nose, after which it invades the olfactory nerve and reaches the brain.
explanation.whyCorrect: Infection begins when water containing the amoeba goes up the nose during diving, swimming, or nasal rinsing. The organism penetrates the nasal mucosa, infects the olfactory nerve, and travels along it into the brain, producing primary amebic meningoencephalitis. Finding motile amebae in the CSF of a patient with recent warm freshwater exposure is the classic picture.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Spread from the middle ear is a route for bacterial meningitis, not for this free-living amoeba.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Naegleria fowleri does not establish a pulmonary focus and does not seed the meninges through the bloodstream.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Swallowing water containing the amoeba does not cause illness; the organism must enter through the nose.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Naegleria fowleri is not acquired by inoculation through broken skin; skin ulcers after an outdoor exposure suggest a different parasite entirely.

questions.stem: Autopsy of a 19-year-old man who died of a rapidly progressive meningoencephalitis one week after water skiing shows amebic trophozoites tracking from the roof of the nasal cavity into the frontal lobes. Which of the following structures did the organism most likely traverse to enter the cranial cavity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cribriform plate

choices.label: B
choices.text: Foramen ovale

choices.label: C
choices.text: Internal acoustic meatus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Jugular foramen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Superior orbital fissure

explanation.summary: Naegleria fowleri follows the olfactory nerve through the cribriform plate to reach the brain.
explanation.whyCorrect: The olfactory nerve filaments pass from the nasal roof into the anterior cranial fossa through the perforations of the cribriform plate. The amoeba uses this pathway to move from the nasal mucosa directly into the frontal lobes, which is why the disease is a meningoencephalitis rather than a simple meningitis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The foramen ovale transmits the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve and is not on the olfactory pathway.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The internal acoustic meatus transmits the facial and vestibulocochlear nerves, far from the nasal roof.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The jugular foramen lies in the posterior cranial fossa and carries the internal jugular vein and lower cranial nerves.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The superior orbital fissure connects the orbit to the middle cranial fossa and does not communicate with the nasal roof.

questions.stem: A county health officer is drafting a public advisory about Naegleria fowleri. Which of the following exposures carries the greatest risk of infection in the United States?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Drinking untreated well water on a rural farm in the fall

choices.label: B
choices.text: Showering in chlorinated municipal tap water in the winter

choices.label: C
choices.text: Swimming in a warm southern freshwater lake in August

choices.label: D
choices.text: Swimming in the ocean surf along the Gulf coast in July

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wading in a cold mountain stream during the early spring

explanation.summary: Cases cluster in warm freshwater in southern states during the summer months.
explanation.whyCorrect: Naegleria fowleri lives in warm bodies of fresh water such as lakes, rivers, and hot springs, and the majority of reported United States cases occur in southern coastal states during summer. A hot August day in a southern lake combines the warm water, the freshwater habitat, and the recreational diving that drives water up the nose.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Drinking water that contains the amoeba does not cause disease, so ingestion of well water is not the risk of concern.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The amoeba is only rarely found in tap water, and properly chlorinated municipal water in winter is a very low-risk exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The organism is found in fresh water rather than in ocean surf.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The organism favors warm water; a cold stream in early spring is a poor habitat for it.

questions.stem: A family learns that the warm spring-fed pond behind their house has tested positive for Naegleria fowleri. Several family members have swallowed pond water while fishing, and none has been ill. Which of the following is the most appropriate counseling?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anyone who swallowed the water should be isolated from young children

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every household member should begin antiparasitic prophylaxis today

choices.label: C
choices.text: Household members should be managed as contacts of a reportable illness

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serum antibody titers should be drawn now and repeated in two weeks

choices.label: E
choices.text: Swallowing water that contains the amoeba does not cause this infection

explanation.summary: Drinking water contaminated with Naegleria fowleri does not cause illness; only nasal entry does.
explanation.whyCorrect: Disease requires the amoeba to be forced up the nose so it can invade the olfactory nerve. Water that is swallowed passes through the gastrointestinal tract without causing infection, so the family needs advice about keeping water out of their noses rather than about ingestion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The infection is not transmitted between people, so isolation serves no purpose.
whyWrongByChoice.B: There is no prophylactic regimen given after a possible environmental exposure to this organism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Person-to-person spread does not occur, so household members are not contacts in any meaningful sense.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Serology is not how this infection is identified; diagnosis rests on visualizing the amoeba, PCR, or antigen detection in CSF or tissue.

questions.stem: A 21-year-old woman is admitted with fever, severe frontal headache, and vomiting. Her family reports that she soaked in a natural hot spring shortly before becoming ill, and primary amebic meningoencephalitis is suspected. Which of the following intervals between nasal exposure and the onset of symptoms is most typical for this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 1 to 7 days, with a median of about 5 days

choices.label: B
choices.text: 2 to 3 months, with a median of about 10 weeks

choices.label: C
choices.text: 2 to 4 weeks, with a median of about 3 weeks

choices.label: D
choices.text: 6 to 12 hours, with a median of about 8 hours

choices.label: E
choices.text: 12 to 36 hours, with a median of about 1 day

explanation.summary: Symptoms of primary amebic meningoencephalitis begin 1 to 7 days after nasal exposure, with a median of about 5 days.
explanation.whyCorrect: The incubation period is short but not immediate: symptoms typically begin within a week of the water exposure, with a median of roughly 5 days. Death usually follows 1 to 18 days after symptoms start, which is why the illness is so often recognized only at autopsy.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A latent period of months is characteristic of other infections, not of this rapidly fatal amebic disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A multi-week incubation period does not fit; most patients are ill within a week of exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An onset within hours is far too rapid for this infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Onset on the first day after exposure is earlier than the typical 1 to 7 day window.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old boy with confirmed primary amebic meningoencephalitis has had a severe frontal headache, fever, nausea, and vomiting for 2 days. Which of the following new findings would indicate that his illness has progressed to the second stage of the disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A generalized seizure followed by altered mental status

choices.label: B
choices.text: A headache that becomes more severe when he lies flat in bed

choices.label: C
choices.text: A temperature that climbs above 39.5 C despite antipyretics

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nausea that returns whenever he attempts to eat solid food

choices.label: E
choices.text: Two further episodes of vomiting after he drinks clear fluids

explanation.summary: Stage 1 of PAM is headache, fever, nausea, and vomiting; stage 2 brings stiff neck, seizures, altered mental status, hallucinations, and coma.
explanation.whyCorrect: The CDC divides the illness into two stages. The first is nonspecific and mimics bacterial meningitis. The second is marked by neurologic deterioration: nuchal rigidity, seizures, confusion or altered mental status, hallucinations, and finally coma. A seizure with a change in mental status therefore marks the transition to stage 2.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Headache is a stage 1 feature; a change in its positional character does not define progression.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fever is present from stage 1 onward, and a higher temperature alone does not mark progression.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nausea is a stage 1 symptom and does not signal neurologic deterioration.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vomiting belongs to stage 1 and its persistence does not indicate a new stage.

questions.stem: A water sample containing Naegleria fowleri trophozoites is transferred from nutrient-rich lake water into cold distilled water. Which of the following changes is most likely to be observed first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conversion of the trophozoites into non-feeding flagellated forms

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fusion of the trophozoites into a large multinucleated syncytium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immediate conversion of the trophozoites into thick-walled cysts

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of all motility with permanent attachment to the flask wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rapid replication of the trophozoites with increased feeding activity

explanation.summary: Adverse conditions first drive Naegleria fowleri from the ameboid trophozoite into a non-feeding flagellate form.
explanation.whyCorrect: The life cycle has three phases: ameboid trophozoite, flagellate, and cyst. When food is scarce or temperatures are extreme, the trophozoite converts into a non-feeding flagellate. Only if the adverse conditions persist does the organism go on to encyst. Despite using flagella in this stage, the organism is still called an amoeba.

whyWrongByChoice.B: This organism does not form a multinucleated syncytium at any point in its life cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Encystment is the later response, occurring only after adverse conditions persist beyond the flagellate stage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The organism retains motility using either pseudopods or flagella depending on its form.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nutrient-poor, cold conditions suppress feeding and replication rather than stimulating them.

questions.stem: The cold, nutrient-poor conditions in that same flask are maintained for several more weeks. Which of the following best describes the form the organism now predominantly takes and its significance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The cyst form, which persists until conditions improve and is not contagious

choices.label: B
choices.text: The cyst form, which spreads between people by the respiratory droplet route

choices.label: C
choices.text: The flagellate form, which is the only stage able to survive in completely dry soil

choices.label: D
choices.text: The flagellate form, which is the stage transmitted directly from person to person

choices.label: E
choices.text: The trophozoite form, which is shed in stool and spreads by the fecal-oral route

explanation.summary: When adverse conditions persist, Naegleria fowleri encysts, and the cyst is a survival form that is not contagious.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cyst is the organism's response to prolonged adverse conditions and allows it to wait until the environment improves, at which point it reverts to the trophozoite. The cyst form is explicitly not contagious, consistent with the fact that this infection is never transmitted between people.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Respiratory droplet spread between people does not occur; infection requires water entering the nose.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The flagellate is a transient, non-feeding swimming form, not a durable survival stage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: There is no person-to-person transmission of this organism in any form.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The trophozoite is not shed in stool, and fecal-oral spread plays no role in this infection.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man is admitted with fever, headache, and confusion 4 days after swimming in a warm lake. Which of the following findings would confirm a diagnosis of Naegleria fowleri infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acid-fast bacilli seen in a cytospin preparation of cerebrospinal fluid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Branching septate hyphae seen on a potassium hydroxide preparation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Budding yeast with a wide clear halo on an India ink preparation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gram-negative diplococci seen on a Gram stain of cerebrospinal fluid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Motile trophozoites seen in a wet preparation of cerebrospinal fluid

explanation.summary: Naegleria fowleri is identified by seeing trophozoites or flagellates in CSF, biopsy, or tissue, or by PCR or antigen detection on those samples.
explanation.whyCorrect: The three standard approaches are direct detection of trophozoites and flagellates in CSF, biopsy, or tissue; detection of parasite nucleic acid by PCR on those same specimens; and detection of parasite antigen using specific antibodies in immunohistochemical testing. Seeing the motile amoeba in spinal fluid establishes the diagnosis at the bedside.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acid-fast bacilli point to mycobacterial disease, not to a free-living amoeba.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Septate hyphae on potassium hydroxide indicate a mold and would not be found in this infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A wide clear halo on India ink indicates an encapsulated yeast, not an amoeba.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gram-negative diplococci indicate bacterial meningitis, the illness this infection is most often confused with.

questions.stem: A hospital reviews a death from primary amebic meningoencephalitis that was recognized only at autopsy. More than three-quarters of these cases in the United States are diagnosed after death, and fewer than 5 of roughly 164 reported patients have survived. Which of the following best explains this pattern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibody titers become detectable only several weeks into recovery

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lumbar puncture is contraindicated once meningeal signs have appeared

choices.label: C
choices.text: The illness is rare and progresses so fast that it is rarely considered

choices.label: D
choices.text: The organism cannot be visualized in cerebrospinal fluid during life

choices.label: E
choices.text: The organism stays confined to brain tissue and never reaches the spinal fluid

explanation.summary: PAM is so rare and so rapidly progressive that it is seldom included in the differential diagnosis while the patient is alive.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because the early symptoms are indistinguishable from bacterial meningitis and the infection kills within 1 to 18 days of symptom onset, clinicians rarely consider it in time. Its rarity compounds the problem: with only about 164 reported cases since 1962 and roughly 98% mortality, it is almost never on the initial differential unless a history of swimming in warm, soil-contaminated water is elicited.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Diagnosis does not depend on antibody titers; direct detection, PCR, and antigen testing are used.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lumbar puncture is how the spinal fluid containing the amoeba is obtained; it is not the obstacle.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trophozoites and flagellates can in fact be seen in cerebrospinal fluid from living patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The organism is recoverable from cerebrospinal fluid as well as from brain tissue.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman at 10 weeks' gestation asks which household chores she should hand off to her husband. The couple keeps one indoor cat. Which of the following activities poses the greatest risk of Toxoplasma gondii infection for her?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Brushing the cat's fur each evening after dinner

choices.label: B
choices.text: Emptying and scrubbing out the cat's litter box

choices.label: C
choices.text: Petting the cat while it sits on her lap at night

choices.label: D
choices.text: Refilling the cat's dry food and water bowls

choices.label: E
choices.text: Washing the cat's blanket in the household machine

explanation.summary: Toxoplasma gondii oocysts are shed in cat feces, so pregnant women should avoid contact with cat litter.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cats release oocysts in their feces, and humans become infected by ingesting food or water contaminated with cat feces. Because the parasite can cross the placenta and infect the fetus, pregnant women are specifically advised to avoid contact with cat feces, which makes litter box duty the exposure to eliminate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Grooming a cat is not the described route of transmission; the parasite is acquired from feces or from meat.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Petting a cat does not transmit the parasite, which is why cat ownership itself need not be avoided.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Handling food and water bowls does not involve contact with cat feces.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Laundering bedding is not a described route of infection for this parasite.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man who has never owned a pet develops 2 weeks of low-grade fever, malaise, and cervical lymphadenopathy. Serology is positive for acute Toxoplasma gondii infection. He reports eating rare lamb and home-butchered venison several times a month. Which of the following best explains how he acquired the infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A bite from an infected female phlebotomine sandfly

choices.label: B
choices.text: Contact with the saliva of an infected neighborhood cat

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ingestion of tissue cysts present in undercooked meat

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhalation of aerosolized oocysts while cleaning out a barn

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transmission during unprotected sexual contact with a partner

explanation.summary: Eating undercooked meat containing tissue cysts is a common route of Toxoplasma gondii infection, independent of cat ownership.
explanation.whyCorrect: Toxoplasma gondii infects a wide range of warm-blooded mammals, and the meat of infected animals contains tissue cysts. Consuming that meat undercooked delivers viable parasites to the gut, and this is one of the two common routes of human infection alongside ingestion of oocysts from cat feces. Healthy adults typically develop a mononucleosis-like illness, as here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sandfly bites transmit Leishmania species, not Toxoplasma gondii.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The parasite is acquired from cat feces, not from cat saliva or casual cat contact.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aerosol inhalation is not a described route of transmission for this parasite.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sexual transmission characterizes Trichomonas vaginalis, not Toxoplasma gondii.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman acquires a primary Toxoplasma gondii infection at 12 weeks' gestation. Which of the following best describes how the fetus becomes infected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amastigotes are carried across the placenta inside maternal neutrophils

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bradyzoites are passed to the newborn in breast milk after the delivery

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oocysts ascend from the vagina through the cervix into the uterine cavity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tachyzoites cross the placenta and reach the fetus through the bloodstream

choices.label: E
choices.text: The fetus swallows oocysts that have been shed into the amniotic fluid

explanation.summary: Toxoplasma gondii is the T in TORCH because tachyzoites cross the placenta and infect the fetus hematogenously.
explanation.whyCorrect: After a pregnant woman is infected, oocysts or tissue cysts transform into tachyzoites, the highly mobile form that disseminates through the bloodstream. Tachyzoites can cross the placenta and infect the fetus, causing miscarriage or a congenital infection that may not become apparent until after birth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amastigotes are a Leishmania stage and have no role in toxoplasmosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Breast milk transmission is not a described route for this parasite.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This parasite does not ascend from the genital tract; that route belongs to sexually transmitted organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oocysts are shed by cats into the environment, not into the amniotic cavity.

questions.stem: A newborn is evaluated for lethargy and an enlarging head circumference. Head CT shows scattered bright calcifications throughout the brain, and the dilated eye examination shows inflammation of the retina and choroid.
