Which of the following triads is classically present in congenital toxoplasmosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cataracts, sensorineural deafness, and patent ductus arteriosus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus, and intracranial calcifications

choices.label: C
choices.text: Conjunctivitis, nasal cartilage destruction, and splenomegaly

choices.label: D
choices.text: Limb hypoplasia, cicatricial skin scarring, and cortical atrophy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Microcephaly, a petechial rash, and massive hepatosplenomegaly

explanation.summary: The classic triad of congenital toxoplasmosis is chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus, and intracranial calcifications.
explanation.whyCorrect: Children born with congenital toxoplasmosis classically show inflammation of the retina and choroid, abnormal enlargement of the brain cavities from cerebrospinal fluid build-up, and calcification within the brain parenchyma. The newborn described has all three components.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This combination points to a different congenital infection and does not include the calcifications and hydrocephalus of toxoplasmosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Destruction of nasal cartilage is a feature of mucocutaneous leishmaniasis, not of congenital toxoplasmosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Limb hypoplasia with scarred skin is not part of the described congenital toxoplasmosis triad.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Microcephaly with a petechial rash is not the triad taught for this parasite; hydrocephalus, not microcephaly, is the classic finding.

questions.stem: A 43-year-old man with HIV infection who stopped taking his antiretroviral medications presents with headaches, confusion, and occasional seizures. His CD4 T-cell count is 75/uL (normal 500-1500). MRI of the brain shows multiple ring-enhancing lesions. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause of his brain lesions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Leishmania braziliensis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Leishmania donovani

choices.label: C
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: D
choices.text: Toxoplasma gondii

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichomonas vaginalis

explanation.summary: Multiple ring-enhancing brain lesions in a patient with AIDS are the classic picture of reactivated toxoplasmosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Once acquired, Toxoplasma gondii persists for life in tissue cysts. Severe immunosuppression, such as a CD4 count below 200/uL, allows reactivation, and lesions form in the affected tissue. The brain is a favored site, and the imaging signature is multiple ring-enhancing lesions accompanied by fever, confusion, headache, and seizures.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This species causes mucocutaneous disease of the nose and face rather than brain lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This species causes visceral leishmaniasis with fever, splenomegaly, and marrow failure rather than brain lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This amoeba causes a fulminant meningoencephalitis after nasal exposure to warm fresh water, not chronic ring-enhancing lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This flagellate causes a sexually transmitted genital infection and does not invade the brain.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly pairs a form of Toxoplasma gondii with its role in human infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amastigote - the form shed in the feces of an infected domestic cat

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bradyzoite - the highly mobile form that carries the parasite through the blood

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oocyst - the dormant form residing within tissue cysts in muscle and brain

choices.label: D
choices.text: Promastigote - the form that develops within human tissue cysts after invasion

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tachyzoite - the rapidly disseminating form that invades and lyses host cells

explanation.summary: In humans Toxoplasma gondii alternates between tachyzoites, the mobile invasive form, and bradyzoites, the dormant form inside tissue cysts.
explanation.whyCorrect: Shortly after ingestion, oocysts transform into tachyzoites that disseminate rapidly, invade host cells, replicate within them, and lyse them. Once embedded in liver, muscle, or brain, the tachyzoites develop into tissue cysts containing bradyzoites, which remain dormant for the life of the host.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The amastigote is a Leishmania tissue stage, and cats shed oocysts rather than amastigotes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The bradyzoite is the dormant tissue-cyst form; the tachyzoite is the highly mobile one.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The oocyst is the form shed in cat feces, not the form found inside tissue cysts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The promastigote is a Leishmania stage injected by sandflies and has no role in toxoplasmosis.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with lifelong latent toxoplasmosis begins high-dose immunosuppression after a kidney transplant. Six weeks later he develops focal neurologic deficits and new brain lesions. Which of the following events best explains his illness?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bradyzoites within dormant tissue cysts converted back into tachyzoites

choices.label: B
choices.text: Circulating immune complexes were deposited within his cerebral capillaries

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dormant tissue cysts ruptured and released oocysts into his bloodstream

choices.label: D
choices.text: Newly swallowed oocysts hatched directly within his central nervous system

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tachyzoites encysted more rapidly and formed enlarging brain granulomas

explanation.summary: Reactivation occurs when bradyzoites in dormant tissue cysts revert to tachyzoites and spread again.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tissue cysts formed at the time of the original infection sit dormant for the life of the host. When the host becomes immunocompromised, the cyst reactivates, the bradyzoites transform back into tachyzoites, and the parasite spreads and forms new cysts. The resulting destructive lesions are particularly damaging in the brain and eyes.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Immune complex deposition does not explain the focal parasitic lesions of reactivated toxoplasmosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cysts contain bradyzoites, not oocysts; oocysts are the environmental form shed by cats.
whyWrongByChoice.D: His disease is reactivation of a latent infection; oocysts are ingested and transform in the gut, not in the brain.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reactivation involves cysts opening and bradyzoites becoming tachyzoites, not accelerated encystment.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old man with AIDS has fever, headache, and ring-enhancing brain lesions. Serum antibody titers against Toxoplasma gondii are not elevated. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in establishing the diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conclude that the negative antibody titer has excluded active toxoplasmosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Defer all testing until immune reconstitution permits a reliable antibody response

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obtain a tissue sample to visualize the parasite or amplify its DNA by PCR

choices.label: D
choices.text: Repeat the serum antibody titer weekly until a fourfold rise is documented

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treat empirically for bacterial meningitis and repeat the brain imaging in a month

explanation.summary: Severely immunocompromised patients may have active toxoplasmosis without elevated antibody titers, so direct visualization or PCR is needed.
explanation.whyCorrect: Serology is the usual first-line test because antibody titers rise during active infection, but a severely immunocompromised patient such as one with AIDS may fail to mount that response despite active disease. In that setting, visualizing the parasite in a tissue sample or amplifying its nucleic acid by PCR carries substantial diagnostic value, and confirmatory testing through a reference laboratory is recommended.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A non-elevated titer does not exclude infection in a severely immunocompromised host; this is the central pitfall being tested.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Delaying diagnosis in a patient with active brain lesions is unsafe and unnecessary when direct testing is available.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A patient who cannot mount an antibody response will not produce a fourfold rise no matter how often the titer is repeated.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ring-enhancing lesions in a patient with AIDS point to toxoplasmosis rather than bacterial meningitis, and empiric antibacterial therapy would not establish the diagnosis.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman at 18 weeks' gestation has serologic evidence of acute toxoplasmosis. Which of the following is the most appropriate test to determine whether the fetus has been infected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Culture of maternal stool for oocysts of the parasite

choices.label: B
choices.text: Giemsa-stained smear of a maternal bone marrow aspirate

choices.label: C
choices.text: PCR for parasite DNA performed on amniotic fluid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Punch biopsy of maternal skin over the anterior forearm

choices.label: E
choices.text: Saline wet preparation of maternal vaginal secretions

explanation.summary: Toxoplasma gondii DNA can be detected by PCR in amniotic fluid when mother-to-child transmission is a concern.
explanation.whyCorrect: In possible congenital transmission, nucleic acid amplification of amniotic fluid is the test that directly addresses whether the parasite has reached the fetal compartment. Maternal serology establishes that the mother is infected but cannot by itself establish fetal infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Humans do not shed oocysts in stool; cats do, so stool testing of the mother is uninformative.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bone marrow aspiration is used to demonstrate Leishmania amastigotes in visceral leishmaniasis, not to diagnose fetal toxoplasmosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Skin biopsy is the sampling approach for cutaneous leishmaniasis and says nothing about fetal infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A vaginal wet mount is the bedside test for Trichomonas vaginalis and has no role here.

questions.stem: A healthy 24-year-old woman has 3 weeks of fever, fatigue, and cervical lymphadenopathy. Heterophile antibody testing is negative and Toxoplasma gondii serology is positive. Which of the following best describes the expected course of her infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Symptoms resolve, but the organism persists for life within tissue cysts

choices.label: B
choices.text: The illness inevitably progresses to encephalitis within several months

choices.label: C
choices.text: The organism is fully cleared, and immunity prevents any cyst formation

choices.label: D
choices.text: The organism is shed in her stool and readily spreads to close contacts

choices.label: E
choices.text: Therapy eradicates the organism entirely, so later reactivation is not possible

explanation.summary: In an immunocompetent host, toxoplasmosis is a self-limited mononucleosis-like illness, but the parasite persists for life in tissue cysts.
explanation.whyCorrect: An immunocompetent host controls the acute infection, and when symptoms occur in healthy adults they resemble mononucleosis. However, tachyzoites that reached the liver, muscle, and brain have already formed tissue cysts containing bradyzoites, and once infected a person has toxoplasmosis for life. That latent reservoir is what reactivates if severe immunosuppression later develops.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Encephalitis is a complication of reactivation in immunocompromised hosts, not the expected course in a healthy adult.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cyst formation has already occurred by the time the acute illness resolves; immunity contains rather than eliminates the parasite.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Humans do not shed this parasite in stool, and person-to-person spread by casual contact does not occur.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The organism is not eradicated; latent tissue cysts persist and can reactivate.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman reports burning with urination and a foul-smelling, frothy yellow-green vaginal discharge. On speculum examination the vaginal walls are inflamed and the cervix shows punctate hemorrhages, giving it a strawberry-like appearance. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Candida albicans

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gardnerella vaginalis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: D
choices.text: Toxoplasma gondii

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichomonas vaginalis

explanation.summary: A frothy yellow-green malodorous discharge with a strawberry cervix is classic trichomoniasis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Trichomonas vaginalis produces an intensely inflammatory vaginitis. The discharge is frothy and yellow to green with a pungent fishy odor, and inflammation of the cervix produces the punctate hemorrhages that give the strawberry cervix its name. Burning with urination is a common accompanying complaint.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Candida vulvovaginitis causes inflammation with a thick, white, cottage-cheese discharge and a normal vaginal pH.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bacterial vaginosis produces a thin white discharge with a fishy odor but characteristically causes no inflammation and no strawberry cervix.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This free-living amoeba causes a fulminant meningoencephalitis and does not infect the genital tract.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This parasite causes congenital disease and reactivation lesions in immunocompromised hosts, not vaginitis.

questions.stem: The vaginal pH of the patient above is 5.5; the normal range is 3.8 to 4.5. Which of the following best explains the elevated pH?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amines produced by the parasite raise the pH of the vaginal fluid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Estrogen withdrawal has depleted glycogen stores in the epithelium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neutrophils recruited to the mucosa acidify the vaginal secretions

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pseudohyphae consume the lactic acid generated by resident lactobacilli

choices.label: E
choices.text: The parasite ferments vaginal glycogen directly into lactic acid

explanation.summary: Trichomonas vaginalis produces amines that raise the vaginal pH above 4.5 and give the discharge its pungent odor.
explanation.whyCorrect: The parasite generates amines, which are basic compounds. They push the vaginal pH above the normal 3.8 to 4.5 range and are responsible for the fishy smell, described as even more pungent or foul than the odor of bacterial vaginosis. A pH above 4.5 is therefore a standard lab finding in trichomoniasis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hormonal glycogen depletion is not the mechanism described for the elevated pH in trichomoniasis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neutrophil influx reflects inflammation but is not what alters the pH in this infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pseudohyphae are a feature of Candida infection, which characteristically leaves the vaginal pH normal.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Producing lactic acid would lower the pH, not raise it; that is the role of normal vaginal flora.

questions.stem: A saline wet mount is prepared from the vaginal discharge of a woman with suspected trichomoniasis. Which of the following findings is expected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A motile pear-shaped organism with four flagella and an undulating membrane

choices.label: B
choices.text: A round cyst with four nuclei enclosed in a smooth, refractile double wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: A slender intracellular organism with a terminal kinetoplast and no flagellum

choices.label: D
choices.text: An epithelial cell whose borders are obscured by densely adherent coccobacilli

choices.label: E
choices.text: Budding yeast forms with branching pseudohyphae and no independent motility

explanation.summary: A wet mount of trichomoniasis shows a highly motile pear-shaped flagellate with four flagella at one end and an undulating membrane.
explanation.whyCorrect: Simple microscopy of vaginal secretions or penile discharge is the standard bedside diagnostic test. Trichomonas vaginalis has four flagella at one end, a single nucleus, and a surrounding membrane that moves in a wave-like motion, giving the characteristic darting motility of a motile pear-shaped trichomonad.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A multinucleate cyst with a refractile wall is not the morphology of this flagellate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An intracellular organism with a kinetoplast describes the Leishmania amastigote seen in phagocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An epithelial cell coated with bacteria is a clue cell, the hallmark of bacterial vaginosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Budding yeast with pseudohyphae indicates Candida vulvovaginitis, which is nonmotile.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman treated with metronidazole for trichomoniasis returns 6 weeks later with the same symptoms. She has one sexual partner, who has no symptoms and was never treated. Which of the following best explains her recurrence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Drug resistance that requires a topical azole agent for her and her partner

choices.label: B
choices.text: Misdiagnosis, because her original symptoms were caused by bacterial vaginosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reinfection acquired from swimming in an inadequately maintained public pool

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reinfection from her untreated partner, who can carry the parasite silently

choices.label: E
choices.text: Relapse from dormant tissue cysts that survived the first course of therapy

explanation.summary: Patients can be reinfected by asymptomatic partners, so sexual partners must be treated even when they have no symptoms.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most people with trichomoniasis have no symptoms yet still spread the parasite. A patient who completes therapy while her partner goes untreated is readily reinfected, which is why the standard approach is to treat the patient and the partners simultaneously regardless of partner symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Azoles are the treatment for Candida vulvovaginitis, and there is no indication here that the organism failed to respond to therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bacterial vaginosis does not cause the inflammatory picture she originally had, and it would not be cured and then recur in this pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This parasite is sexually transmitted; it is not acquired from recreational water.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trichomonas vaginalis does not form dormant tissue cysts; latent cysts are a feature of Toxoplasma gondii.

questions.stem: The asymptomatic male partner of a woman with trichomoniasis asks whether he could really be infected when he feels completely well. Which of the following statements is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Having no symptoms two weeks after exposure reliably excludes infection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Men are not colonized by this parasite and require no further evaluation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nearly all infected men develop penile burning within a week of exposure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only about 30% of people who acquire this infection develop any symptoms

choices.label: E
choices.text: Roughly 90% of people who acquire this infection develop symptoms promptly

explanation.summary: Only about 30% of people who contract trichomoniasis ever develop symptoms, and asymptomatic people still transmit the parasite.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most infected people are asymptomatic; roughly 30% develop symptoms, and it is not understood why some do and others do not. Untreated infection can persist for months to years and be transmitted throughout, which is why an asymptomatic partner still needs treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Absence of symptoms at any time point does not exclude infection with this organism.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Men are infected and transmit the parasite, so partner evaluation and treatment are essential.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Men can be infected without symptoms; when symptoms do occur they include penile burning worsened by urination or ejaculation and a thick discharge.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This reverses the true proportion; the large majority of infections are asymptomatic.

questions.stem: Two women present with a malodorous vaginal discharge. Both have a vaginal pH of 5.0 and both describe the odor as fishy. Which of the following findings best distinguishes trichomoniasis from bacterial vaginosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A discharge that has been present for more than two weeks before presentation

choices.label: B
choices.text: A discharge that the patient notices more in the days after intercourse

choices.label: C
choices.text: A vaginal pH measured above 4.5 on a sample of the pooled discharge

choices.label: D
choices.text: An odor that the patient herself describes as fishy or foul smelling

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inflammation of the vaginal walls and cervix on speculum examination

explanation.summary: Both infections raise vaginal pH above 4.5 and smell fishy, but only trichomoniasis produces inflammation, including the strawberry cervix.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the standard comparison of vaginal infections, bacterial vaginosis is listed as causing no inflammation with a thin white discharge, whereas trichomoniasis causes visible inflammation of the vaginal walls and cervix with punctate hemorrhages. Because both share a pH above 4.5 and a fishy odor, the presence of inflammation is the discriminating examination finding.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both infections can persist for weeks or longer, so duration does not distinguish them.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Changes in discharge around intercourse are nonspecific and occur with either condition.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A pH above 4.5 occurs in both conditions and therefore cannot separate them.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A fishy odor is reported in both, although the trichomonal odor tends to be more pungent; it is not a reliable discriminator.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman has vulvar itching and a thick, white, clumpy discharge. The vulva and vagina are inflamed, the vaginal pH is 4.2, and microscopy of the discharge shows pseudohyphae. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A single antiparasitic dose given to both the patient and her partner

choices.label: B
choices.text: An azole antifungal agent for the patient alone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Metronidazole for the patient and for all of her sexual partners

choices.label: D
choices.text: Metronidazole or clindamycin for the patient alone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Observation alone, because this vaginal pH excludes any infection

explanation.summary: Thick white cottage-cheese discharge with pseudohyphae and a normal vaginal pH is Candida vulvovaginitis, treated with azoles.
explanation.whyCorrect: Candida vulvovaginitis is the one common vaginal infection in which the pH stays in the normal 4.0 to 4.5 range. It produces inflammation with a thick, white, cottage-cheese discharge, and pseudohyphae are the diagnostic microscopic finding. Azoles are the treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antiparasitic therapy with partner treatment addresses a sexually transmitted protozoan, not a yeast.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Metronidazole with partner treatment is the regimen for trichomoniasis, which produces a frothy yellow-green discharge and a pH above 4.5.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Metronidazole or clindamycin treats bacterial vaginosis, which causes a thin white discharge with clue cells and no inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The normal pH is expected in candidiasis and does not rule out infection; the pseudohyphae confirm it.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman at 20 weeks' gestation is diagnosed with trichomoniasis. Which of the following outcomes is she at increased risk for?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fetal hydrocephalus with scattered intracranial calcifications

choices.label: B
choices.text: Neonatal chorioretinitis discovered in the first month of life

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neonatal meningoencephalitis within the first week of life

choices.label: D
choices.text: Preterm delivery of an infant with a low birth weight

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spontaneous miscarriage during the first trimester of pregnancy

explanation.summary: Trichomoniasis in pregnancy is associated with early delivery and low birth weight.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pregnant women with trichomoniasis are more likely to deliver early and to have infants with low birth weights, which is one reason consistent prenatal care matters for both mother and child. This is a distinct risk profile from the congenital infections caused by organisms that cross the placenta.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hydrocephalus with intracranial calcifications belongs to the congenital toxoplasmosis triad.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chorioretinitis in a newborn points to congenital toxoplasmosis, which crosses the placenta.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neonatal meningoencephalitis is not an outcome attributed to this sexually transmitted flagellate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: First-trimester miscarriage is the outcome associated with Toxoplasma gondii crossing the placenta.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man returns from hiking and biking through the Brazilian countryside with a slowly enlarging, scabbed ulcer with a raised border on his forearm. He is afebrile and otherwise well. He recalls multiple bug bites but never saw what bit him. Which of the following vectors most likely transmitted his infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A female Anopheles mosquito feeding at dusk

choices.label: B
choices.text: A female phlebotomine sandfly biting at night

choices.label: C
choices.text: A hard-bodied tick attached for more than a day

choices.label: D
choices.text: A reduviid bug feeding near the eyes at night

choices.label: E
choices.text: A tsetse fly biting during the daylight hours

explanation.summary: Leishmania species are transmitted by the bite of infected female phlebotomine sandflies.
explanation.whyCorrect: The genus Leishmania consists of obligate intracellular protozoans transmitted by infected female phlebotomine sandflies. Sandflies are very small and feed at night on sleeping people, so patients rarely notice being bitten and rarely report the exposure, exactly as in this traveler who recalls only nonspecific bug bites.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mosquito-borne parasitic illness in a returning traveler suggests malaria, which presents with fever rather than a chronic skin ulcer.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ticks are not the vector for this parasite.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reduviid bugs transmit a different protozoan and are not the vector discussed for this ulcer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tsetse flies are not the vector for Leishmania species.

questions.stem: Biopsy of that forearm ulcer shows parasites inside phagocytes in the dermis. Which of the following best describes how the parasite reached this location?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amastigotes penetrated intact skin on their own and entered dermal capillaries directly

choices.label: B
choices.text: Amastigotes were injected by the vector and converted into promastigotes in the skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Promastigotes were injected by the vector and encysted within the dermal fibroblasts

choices.label: D
choices.text: Promastigotes were injected by the vector and multiplied freely in the extracellular space

choices.label: E
choices.text: Promastigotes were injected by the vector, were phagocytosed, and became amastigotes

explanation.summary: The sandfly injects flagellated promastigotes, which are phagocytosed and transform into amastigotes inside macrophages.
explanation.whyCorrect: The promastigote, which bears a long flagellum, is the infectious form injected into the skin during the sandfly bite. It is phagocytosed predominantly by macrophages and other phagocytic cells, including neutrophils, then avoids being killed inside the phagocyte and transforms into the amastigote, the tissue form. Seeing amastigotes within phagocytes on biopsy confirms the diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The parasite does not penetrate intact skin on its own; it requires inoculation by the vector.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The direction is reversed: promastigotes are injected and become amastigotes in the host, while the reverse conversion happens inside the sandfly.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Leishmania does not form cysts in fibroblasts; it survives as an amastigote within phagocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Leishmania species are obligate intracellular parasites and do not multiply freely outside host cells.

questions.stem: The traveler above is told that his ulcer represents the most common clinical form of leishmaniasis. Which of the following best describes the expected course of an uncomplicated lesion of this type?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It almost always progresses to fatal systemic disease if untreated

choices.label: B
choices.text: It persists unchanged for the patient's life unless surgically excised

choices.label: C
choices.text: It typically heals within a week but then recurs every few months

choices.label: D
choices.text: It usually heals on its own over a period of 2 to 15 months

choices.label: E
choices.text: It usually resolves completely within 5 to 7 days of its onset

explanation.summary: Cutaneous leishmaniasis is the most common form and its lesions typically heal on their own over 2 to 15 months.
explanation.whyCorrect: Roughly 1.5 million of the 2 million new cases of leishmaniasis each year are cutaneous. Infected bite sites start as a papule or nodule, may advance into an ulcer that scabs over with a raised border, and are often accompanied by swollen glands near the bite. These lesions typically heal themselves over 2 to 15 months, with recovery time varying by species.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Systemic spread is rare; most cutaneous cases are self-limiting skin ulcers.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The lesions generally heal spontaneously rather than persisting indefinitely.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A weekly heal-and-relapse pattern does not describe cutaneous leishmaniasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Resolution within a week is far faster than the months-long course of these ulcers.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy in rural East Africa has had intermittent fevers for 2 months. He is cachectic, with massive splenomegaly and an enlarged liver. Hemoglobin is 6.2 g/dL and the leukocyte count is markedly low. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cutaneous leishmaniasis that has disseminated across the skin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mucocutaneous leishmaniasis caused by Leishmania braziliensis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Primary amebic meningoencephalitis caused by Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reactivated toxoplasmosis caused by Toxoplasma gondii

choices.label: E
choices.text: Visceral leishmaniasis caused by Leishmania donovani

explanation.summary: Visceral leishmaniasis, or kala-azar, is caused mainly by L. donovani and L. infantum and presents with prolonged fever, splenomegaly, anemia, and leukopenia.
explanation.whyCorrect: After multiplying in macrophages at the bite site, these two species spread systemically and infect phagocytes in the spleen, bone marrow, liver, and lymph nodes. Severe fever that waxes and wanes for weeks is the most common feature, with splenomegaly and hepatomegaly appearing later and marrow involvement producing severe anemia and leukopenia. Untreated, almost every case is fatal.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Disseminated cutaneous disease spreads lesions across the skin rather than invading the spleen and marrow.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Mucocutaneous disease destroys nasal and oropharyngeal tissue and does not cause splenomegaly with marrow failure.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This amoeba causes an abrupt fatal meningoencephalitis, not months of fever with organomegaly.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reactivated toxoplasmosis produces destructive brain and eye lesions in immunocompromised hosts, not this hematologic picture.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old man who spent his twenties in the Amazon basin had a skin ulcer on his leg that healed about 9 years ago. He now has recurrent nosebleeds, progressive destruction of his nasal cartilage, and difficulty swallowing. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Leishmania braziliensis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Leishmania donovani

choices.label: C
choices.text: Leishmania infantum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Toxoplasma gondii

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichomonas vaginalis

explanation.summary: Mucocutaneous leishmaniasis, most often caused by L. braziliensis, follows cutaneous disease and destroys the nose and upper airway.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mucocutaneous disease can occur during cutaneous leishmaniasis or years afterward, with some patients presenting a full decade after the primary ulcer. It typically begins as nosebleeds and progresses to destruction of nasal cartilage, with the pharynx and larynx impairing swallowing and the lips, cheeks, and soft palate frequently involved. Cases are most common in South America, and L. braziliensis is the most common etiologic agent.

whyWrongByChoice.B: This species is one of the two main causes of visceral disease with fever and splenomegaly.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This species also causes visceral disease rather than destructive mucosal lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This parasite causes congenital disease and reactivation lesions of the brain and eyes, not nasal destruction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This flagellate causes a sexually transmitted genital infection and does not involve the nasal mucosa.

questions.stem: A physician plans to confirm visceral leishmaniasis by demonstrating the parasite in a patient sample. Splenic aspiration has the highest sensitivity, exceeding 95%, yet a bone marrow aspirate is usually obtained instead. Which of the following best explains this choice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bone marrow aspiration is more sensitive than splenic aspiration for this parasite

choices.label: B
choices.text: Splenic aspirates cannot be interpreted once the spleen has become enlarged

choices.label: C
choices.text: Splenic aspirates require culture, whereas marrow can be examined microscopically

choices.label: D
choices.text: Splenic aspiration carries a substantial risk of serious hemorrhage

choices.label: E
choices.text: The parasite infects marrow phagocytes but is entirely absent from the spleen

explanation.summary: Spleen samples are the most sensitive for visceral leishmaniasis, but the bleeding risk means bone marrow is commonly substituted.
explanation.whyCorrect: The gold standard for diagnosing leishmaniasis is observing the pathogen in a patient sample. For visceral disease, splenic samples yield the best results with greater than 95% sensitivity, but because of the risk of hemorrhaging, bone marrow samples are commonly substituted. Whole blood and lymph nodes are less sensitive but even less invasive alternatives.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The spleen is the more sensitive site; the marrow is chosen for safety, not for yield.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Splenomegaly is a typical feature of the disease and does not render the aspirate uninterpretable.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Both sample types can be examined microscopically for amastigotes within phagocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The parasite infects phagocytes in the spleen, bone marrow, liver, and lymph nodes alike.

questions.stem: A traveler returning from an endemic region has a positive serologic test for Leishmania. Which of the following best explains why this result is of limited diagnostic value?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibodies against the parasite appear only after the infection has been treated

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antibody production requires cell-mediated immunity, which the infection destroys

choices.label: C
choices.text: The assay turns positive only in visceral disease and never in cutaneous disease

choices.label: D
choices.text: The serologic assay cross-reacts with antibodies directed against Toxoplasma gondii

choices.label: E
choices.text: Titers are high in many healthy people and cannot separate current from past infection

explanation.summary: Leishmania serology is unreliable because subclinical infection is widespread and antibodies persist after the infection resolves.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antibody titers against Leishmania species are high even in healthy individuals in endemic areas because subclinical infections are so common. Serology also cannot distinguish a current infection from a recent one that has already resolved. For these reasons diagnosis rests on visualizing the parasite, with molecular techniques and PCR used to confirm the species.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antibodies are present during infection; the problem is that they are also present in people without disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Antibody responses are in fact robust in leishmaniasis, including in disseminated cutaneous disease with a Th2-polarized response.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Antibody titers are not confined to visceral disease; the difficulty is their poor specificity for active infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cross-reaction with a different protozoan is not the stated limitation of this assay.

questions.stem: Global mortality data from parasitic disease are being reviewed. Visceral leishmaniasis, also called kala-azar, ranks second among parasitic infections as a cause of death worldwide. Which of the following parasitic diseases ranks first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cutaneous leishmaniasis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Malaria

choices.label: C
choices.text: Primary amebic meningoencephalitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Toxoplasmosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichomoniasis

explanation.summary: Visceral leishmaniasis is the second most common cause of death globally from a parasitic infection, behind only malaria.
explanation.whyCorrect: Visceral leishmaniasis, known as kala-azar or black fever, is nearly uniformly fatal when untreated, and its global death toll is exceeded only by that of malaria. This ranking underscores why systemic spread in a person with a weakened immune system is the feared outcome of Leishmania infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cutaneous disease is the most common form of leishmaniasis but its lesions typically heal on their own.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This infection is almost always fatal for the individual but is exceedingly rare, with only about 164 reported United States cases since 1962.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Most toxoplasmosis is asymptomatic and lifelong; deaths are concentrated in immunocompromised and congenitally infected patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trichomoniasis is extremely common but is not a leading cause of death.

questions.stem: A 37-year-old woman has a 3-month history of abdominal discomfort, increasing fatigue, and intermittent diarrhea. Over the past year she has stopped eating red meat and now eats fresh fish several times a week, including sushi and ceviche. Serum vitamin B12 concentration is low. Stool examination shows large, oval eggs with an operculum at one pole. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diphyllobothrium latum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taenia asiatica

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taenia saginata

choices.label: E
choices.text: Taenia solium

explanation.summary: Raw freshwater fish plus low vitamin B12 plus large oval operculated eggs in stool is diphyllobothriasis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Diphyllobothrium latum, the fish tapeworm, is acquired by eating raw or undercooked fish that contains the plerocercoid larva. Its eggs are oval with a small lid, the operculum, at one end and sometimes a slight knob at the other. A history of raw fish together with low B12 points to this infection, and finding these eggs in stool supports the diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: This is a free-living amoeba that causes rapidly fatal central nervous system disease, not an intestinal helminth that sheds eggs in stool.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The Asian tapeworm is a pork-associated Taenia found only in Asia, and its eggs are the same round, striated Taenia eggs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The beef tapeworm is acquired from undercooked beef and sheds round eggs with a striated outer membrane, not operculated oval eggs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The pork tapeworm is acquired from undercooked pork and also sheds round, striated eggs rather than operculated ones.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man has a 3-week history of moderate abdominal discomfort and infrequent diarrhea. He follows a fad "primal diet" and regularly eats raw beef. A tapeworm infection is suspected and stool microscopy is performed. Which of the following findings is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Encysted larvae within fragments of striated muscle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oval eggs bearing an operculum at one pole

choices.label: C
choices.text: Proglottids with a rosette-shaped central uterus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Round eggs with striations around the outer membrane

choices.label: E
choices.text: Worm segments whose scolex bears two grooves

explanation.summary: All Taenia species shed round eggs with a striated outer membrane; raw beef points to T. saginata.
explanation.whyCorrect: Eating raw or undercooked beef transmits Taenia saginata. The eggs of every Taenia species are round and carry striations, or fine lines, all around the outer membrane, and small hooks can occasionally be seen inside the egg. These eggs confirm taeniasis but cannot identify the species.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cysticerci sit in the muscle of infected cattle and pigs; they are not a finding in a human stool specimen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An operculated oval egg is the egg of Diphyllobothrium spp., which is acquired from raw fish rather than beef.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A rosette-shaped central uterus is the distinguishing feature of Diphyllobothrium proglottids, not Taenia proglottids.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Two grooves, the bothria, are found on the Diphyllobothrium scolex, not on a beef tapeworm.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old woman has a first generalized seizure. She has no history of head trauma or prior neurologic disease. MRI of the brain shows multiple calcified lesions scattered through both cerebral hemispheres. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diphyllobothrium latum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taenia saginata

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taenia solium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wuchereria bancrofti

explanation.summary: Seizures with multiple calcified brain lesions are the classic picture of neurocysticercosis from Taenia solium.
explanation.whyCorrect: Taenia solium is the only tapeworm in this brick whose eggs hatch after a human swallows them. The released larvae invade the intestinal wall, enter the bloodstream, and seed tissues including the brain, where they mature into cysticerci. The resulting inflammation leaves calcified lesions, and seizures are the most common presentation of neurocysticercosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The fish tapeworm stays in the lumen of the small intestine and does not invade tissue or reach the brain.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This amoeba causes a fulminant meningitis; patients do not live long enough for calcified lesions to form.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Its eggs do not hatch when swallowed by humans, so it causes intestinal disease only and never tissue cysts.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This filarial nematode causes lymphatic filariasis, not calcified intracranial lesions.

questions.stem: Humans are described as the definitive host for Taenia saginata, Taenia solium, and Taenia asiatica. Which of the following best describes what makes a host the definitive host for a parasite?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The parasite completes only larval development in it

choices.label: B
choices.text: The parasite forms tissue cysts in its skeletal muscle

choices.label: C
choices.text: The parasite is delivered to it by an arthropod vector

choices.label: D
choices.text: The parasite lives in it without ever causing disease

choices.label: E
choices.text: The parasite reaches adulthood and sexual maturity in it

explanation.summary: The definitive host is where the parasite matures sexually and lays its eggs.
explanation.whyCorrect: A definitive host is the host in which the parasite reaches adulthood and sexual maturity and lays eggs. For all three Taenia species, humans fill that role: the swallowed cysticercus matures into an adult worm that attaches to the intestine with its scolex and sheds eggs and gravid proglottids in stool.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Supporting only larval development is exactly what defines the intermediate host, not the definitive host.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Forming cysticerci in muscle is what happens in the intermediate host, which for these tapeworms is cattle or pigs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Taenia has no arthropod vector; it is acquired by eating undercooked meat containing cysticerci.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Whether infection causes symptoms is unrelated to host classification; most taeniasis is mild but humans remain definitive hosts.

questions.stem: A public health officer is mapping the global distribution of the three tapeworms that cause taeniasis. Which of the following statements about their geographic distribution is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All three species are evenly distributed worldwide

choices.label: B
choices.text: All three species are restricted to Asia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taenia asiatica is restricted to Asia, the others worldwide

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taenia saginata is restricted to Asia, the others worldwide

choices.label: E
choices.text: Taenia solium is restricted to Asia, the others worldwide

explanation.summary: T. saginata and T. solium occur worldwide, while T. asiatica is found only in Asia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Taenia saginata and Taenia solium are found worldwide but are more prevalent in poorer countries where people live in close contact with pigs and cattle. Taenia asiatica, the Asian tapeworm, is found in Asia only.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Distribution is not even; the beef and pork tapeworms concentrate where people live closely with cattle and pigs.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Only Taenia asiatica is limited to Asia; the other two species occur on every continent.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The beef tapeworm is worldwide in distribution, not confined to Asia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The pork tapeworm is found worldwide; it is Taenia asiatica that is restricted to Asia.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man has intestinal infection with Taenia solium. His physician warns him that he faces a complication that patients with Taenia saginata do not face. Which of the following properties of Taenia solium accounts for this difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Its adult worm grows far longer than that of T. saginata

choices.label: B
choices.text: Its eggs hatch when swallowed by a human and invade tissue

choices.label: C
choices.text: Its eggs survive for years rather than months outdoors

choices.label: D
choices.text: Its gravid proglottids hold more uterine branches per side

choices.label: E
choices.text: Its scolex anchors more deeply into the intestinal mucosa

explanation.summary: Only Taenia solium eggs hatch in humans, which is why only it causes cysticercosis and autoinfection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Unlike T. saginata and T. asiatica, the eggs of T. solium hatch when consumed by humans and treat us the same way they treat pigs. The released oncospheres invade the intestinal wall, enter the blood, and form cysticerci in tissue. Because a patient who carries an adult worm can swallow his own eggs, this also produces autoinfection with repeated reinfection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adult T. solium worms are 2 to 7 m long, shorter than T. saginata, which is usually 5 m or less but may reach 25 m.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Taenia eggs survive days to months in the environment, and egg durability does not confer tissue invasion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: T. solium proglottids carry 7 to 13 lateral branches per side, fewer than the 12 to 30 of T. saginata.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Both species attach with suckers on the scolex, and depth of attachment has nothing to do with tissue invasion.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman who has been a strict vegetarian since childhood has new-onset seizures, and MRI shows several cystic and calcified lesions in the brain. She lives with relatives who recently emigrated from a rural area where pigs roam freely. Which of the following best explains how she acquired this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: She ate undercooked beef containing cysticerci from a cow

choices.label: B
choices.text: She ate undercooked pork containing cysticerci as a child

choices.label: C
choices.text: She drank lake water holding larvae shed by crustaceans

choices.label: D
choices.text: She swallowed tapeworm eggs shed by an infected household member

choices.label: E
choices.text: She was bitten by an insect that inoculated larvae in blood

explanation.summary: Cysticercosis follows swallowing T. solium eggs from human feces, not from eating meat.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tissue cysts come from swallowing T. solium eggs, which are shed in the stool of someone carrying an adult worm. Trace amounts of feces reach food and surfaces such as door handles and tables when handwashing is poor, so a person who has never eaten pork can still acquire cysticercosis from a household contact or food handler.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Beef transmits T. saginata, whose eggs do not hatch in humans, so it cannot produce brain cysts.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Swallowing cysticerci in meat produces an adult worm in the intestine, that is taeniasis, and she has never eaten pork.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Larval stages in crustaceans belong to the fish tapeworm, which never invades human tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Taenia has no arthropod vector; transmission is by eating cysticerci in meat or by the fecal-oral route.

questions.stem: A patient with taeniasis passes an intact adult worm. Examination of the head of the worm shows suckers together with a rostellum carrying two rows of hooks. Which of the following is the most likely species?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diphyllobothrium latum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taenia saginata

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taenia solium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wuchereria bancrofti

explanation.summary: A rostellum with two rows of hooks identifies the scolex of Taenia solium.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because the eggs of all Taenia species look alike, species identification depends on the passed proglottids or the adult worm. The scolex of T. solium carries four suckers plus a rostellum armed with two rows of hooks, which distinguishes it from the other tapeworms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The fish tapeworm scolex has two grooves called bothria rather than suckers and hooks.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This is a free-living amoeba, not a helminth, so it has no scolex at all.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The beef tapeworm scolex has four large suckers but no rostellum and no hooks.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This is a filarial nematode that causes lymphatic filariasis; it has no scolex.

questions.stem: An adult tapeworm recovered from a patient's stool has a scolex with four large suckers but no rostellum and no hooks. Which of the following is the most likely species?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diphyllobothrium latum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taenia saginata

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taenia solium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wuchereria bancrofti

explanation.summary: Four large suckers with no rostellum and no hooks identify Taenia saginata.
explanation.whyCorrect: The scolex of T. saginata bears four large suckers and lacks both a rostellum and hooks. Since the eggs of all Taenia species are essentially identical, this feature of the recovered adult worm is what allows the beef tapeworm to be named.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The fish tapeworm attaches with two grooves, the bothria, and has no suckers.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This is an amoeba rather than a worm, so it has no scolex.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The pork tapeworm carries a rostellum with two rows of hooks in addition to its suckers.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This is a filarial nematode; it has no scolex and does not live in the intestinal lumen.

questions.stem: A gravid proglottid recovered from a patient's stool is examined. Approximately 20 lateral uterine branches are counted on each side of the central uterine stem. Which of the following is the most likely species?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diphyllobothrium latum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taenia saginata

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taenia solium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wuchereria bancrofti

explanation.summary: Taenia saginata gravid proglottids have 12 to 30 lateral uterine branches per side.
explanation.whyCorrect: The number of uterine branches in a gravid proglottid separates the two main Taenia species. T. saginata has 12 to 30 lateral branches on each side of the proglottid, so a count near 20 fits the beef tapeworm.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The fish tapeworm proglottid has a rosette-shaped central uterus instead of counted lateral branches.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This is a single-celled amoeba and produces no proglottids of any kind.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The pork tapeworm has only 7 to 13 lateral branches on each side of a gravid proglottid.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This filarial nematode has no proglottids, so branch counting does not apply.

questions.stem: A gravid proglottid passed by a patient with taeniasis is examined and shows about 9 lateral uterine branches on each side. Which of the following is the most likely species?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diphyllobothrium latum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taenia saginata

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taenia solium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wuchereria bancrofti

explanation.summary: Taenia solium gravid proglottids have only 7 to 13 lateral uterine branches per side.
explanation.whyCorrect: T. solium contains 7 to 13 lateral branches on each side of the gravid proglottid, a lower count than T. saginata. Identifying the species matters here because only T. solium can go on to cause cysticercosis and neurocysticercosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The fish tapeworm proglottid shows a rosette-shaped central uterus, not branches to be counted.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This amoeba is not a worm and produces no proglottids.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The beef tapeworm has 12 to 30 lateral branches per side, well above the count described.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This filarial nematode has no proglottids and lives in lymphatics rather than the gut.

questions.stem: A patient passes a mass of worm segments. Microscopy shows that each segment contains a central uterus arranged so that it resembles a rosette of flower petals. Which of the following is the most likely organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diphyllobothrium latum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taenia saginata

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taenia solium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wuchereria bancrofti

explanation.summary: A rosette-shaped central uterus in the proglottid distinguishes Diphyllobothrium from Taenia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Diphyllobothrium proglottids have central uteruses that look like flower petals, a rosette shape. This is the feature used to tell Diphyllobothrium spp. apart from Taenia spp. when segments are recovered from stool, since the eggs alone cannot separate Diphyllobothrium species from one another.

whyWrongByChoice.B: This free-living amoeba is not a segmented worm and forms no proglottids.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Beef tapeworm gravid proglottids show 12 to 30 lateral uterine branches per side.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pork tapeworm gravid proglottids show 7 to 13 lateral uterine branches per side, not a rosette.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This nematode does not form proglottids; it causes lymphatic filariasis.

questions.stem: The adult fish tapeworm anchors itself to the wall of the small intestine. Which of the following structures does it use to attach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A rosette-shaped uterus within each gravid segment

choices.label: B
choices.text: A rostellum armed with two rows of curved hooks

choices.label: C
choices.text: An operculum set at one pole of the shed egg

choices.label: D
choices.text: Four muscular suckers spaced around the scolex

choices.label: E
choices.text: Two longitudinal grooves on the scolex called bothria

explanation.summary: Diphyllobothrium attaches with two grooves on the scolex called bothria, the source of its name.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the adult form, Diphyllobothrium spp. have two grooves on the scolex called bothria, and the name Diphyllobothrium literally means two grooves. The worm attaches to the small intestine with these bothria, and because they are its only point of tissue contact, the immune system tolerates the worm well and most patients have few symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The rosette uterus is a diagnostic feature of the proglottid and plays no role in attachment.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A rostellum with two rows of hooks belongs to the scolex of Taenia solium.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The operculum is a small lid on the egg and has nothing to do with attaching to the gut.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Four suckers characterize the Taenia scolex; the fish tapeworm has none.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man develops diphyllobothriasis several weeks after eating raw salmon caught in a freshwater lake. Which of the following stages of the parasite did he most likely ingest?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coracidium swimming freely in fresh lake water

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cysticercus lying within striated skeletal muscle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Embryonated egg passed in the feces of a human

choices.label: D
choices.text: Plerocercoid larva within the flesh of the fish

choices.label: E
choices.text: Procercoid larva within a freshwater crustacean

explanation.summary: The plerocercoid in large fish is the stage infectious to humans.
explanation.whyCorrect: The form of the parasite present in infected fish is the plerocercoid. Once a human eats the plerocercoid, it develops into an adult worm in the small intestine. Large fish such as perch, salmon, and whitefish acquire plerocercoids by eating smaller infected fish, and cooking the fish destroys the parasite.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Coracidia hatch from eggs in water and are taken up by crustaceans; they do not infect humans.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cysticerci are the larval stage of Taenia in pigs and cattle, not a stage of the fish tapeworm.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Eggs passed in feces are not infectious to humans; nothing happens if they are swallowed.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The procercoid develops in the freshwater crustacean, the first intermediate host, which people do not eat.

questions.stem: Stool from a patient with abdominal discomfort contains round eggs with a striated outer membrane. The laboratory reports "Taenia species" without naming a species. Which of the following best explains this report?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Molecular testing alone can confirm the genus as Taenia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Routine stool fixatives destroy the features used for naming

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serologic testing must be done before eggs can be reported

choices.label: D
choices.text: The eggs must first be cultured before a species is assigned

choices.label: E
choices.text: The eggs of all Taenia species are essentially identical

explanation.summary: Taenia eggs confirm taeniasis but look alike across species, so species identification needs proglottids or the adult worm.
explanation.whyCorrect: The eggs of all Taenia species are almost identical. They confirm taeniasis but cannot tell you which species is causing the infection. Only by observing the passed proglottids, where uterine branches are counted, or the adult worm, where the scolex is examined, can the correct species be determined.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The genus is already evident from the round, striated egg; the limitation lies at the species level.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Taenia eggs are readily seen and their striations preserved on routine stool microscopy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Serology is used when cysticercosis is suspected, not to report eggs seen in stool.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Helminth eggs are identified by morphology; they are not grown in culture.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man from a rural farming community has new focal neurologic deficits, and CT of the head shows several calcified intracranial lesions. Cysticercosis is suspected. Which of the following is the preferred laboratory test?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Counting lateral uterine branches on a passed proglottid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Culture of cerebrospinal fluid for the causative helminth

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immunoassay for antibodies against Taenia solium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Polymerase chain reaction on stool for Diphyllobothrium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stool examination for round eggs with a striated membrane

explanation.summary: In suspected cysticercosis the preferred test is an immunoassay for antibodies against T. solium, run on blood or CSF.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cysticercosis is usually suspected on the basis of physical examination, history, and imaging of the brain or limbs that shows calcified lesions of old cysts. The preferred confirmatory test is an immunoassay detecting antibodies against T. solium, and it can be performed on blood and/or CSF. Tissue biopsy can also identify cysticerci directly.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Counting uterine branches names an adult worm species and says nothing about cysts in tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Helminths are not recovered by culture, so no culture medium will grow this parasite.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Stool PCR is used for diphyllobothriasis, an infection confined to the gut that never reaches the brain.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A stool exam looks for an adult intestinal worm, and many patients with tissue cysts carry no adult worm.

questions.stem: A patient with suspected neurocysticercosis has a positive serum immunoassay for antibodies against Taenia solium. Which of the following is the most important limitation of this result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It can be interpreted only alongside a tissue biopsy

choices.label: B
choices.text: It cannot separate past infection from current infection

choices.label: C
choices.text: It cannot separate T. solium from T. saginata infection

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is positive only while adult worms remain in the gut

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is valid only when run on CSF rather than on blood

explanation.summary: The cysticercosis immunoassay detects antibody, so it cannot tell a past infection from an active one.
explanation.whyCorrect: The immunoassay detects antibodies against T. solium and does not have the ability to differentiate between past and current infections. A positive result therefore has to be interpreted together with the history, examination, and imaging findings rather than taken as proof of active disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tissue biopsy is a separate, alternative way to find cysticerci, not a requirement for reading the assay.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The assay is directed at T. solium, and T. saginata does not cause tissue cysts in the first place.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cysticercosis often occurs without any adult worm in the gut, so intestinal infection is not needed for a positive result.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The assay can be performed on the blood and/or the CSF, so serum is an acceptable specimen.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man ate undercooked pork 6 weeks ago and is worried he has a tapeworm. He has mild abdominal discomfort. Stool examination performed today shows no eggs and no proglottids. Which of the following best explains this result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At least 3 months pass before eggs or proglottids appear

choices.label: B
choices.text: Eggs reach the stool only after the adult worm dies

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only patients with very heavy worm burdens shed eggs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Swallowed cysticerci are killed by gastric acid within weeks

choices.label: E
choices.text: Taenia eggs are shed only during the first week of infection

explanation.summary: After swallowing a Taenia cysticercus it takes at least 3 months before eggs or proglottids show up in stool.
explanation.whyCorrect: After consumption of the cyst of a Taenia species, it takes at least 3 months before eggs or proglottids are passed in the stool. A single negative stool examination at 6 weeks therefore does not exclude infection, and the study should be repeated later.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The living adult sheds eggs and gravid proglottids continuously; death of the worm is not required.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A single adult worm produces thousands of eggs a day regardless of how many worms are present.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cysticerci survive passage through the stomach and mature into adult worms attached to the intestine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Shedding begins once the worm matures and then continues for as long as the worm lives, which can be years.

questions.stem: After a person swallows Taenia solium eggs, the larvae hatch, penetrate the intestinal wall, enter the bloodstream, and travel to muscle and brain. Approximately how long does it take them to mature into cysticerci?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 5 to 10 years

choices.label: B
choices.text: 5 to 7 days

choices.label: C
choices.text: 6 to 12 months

choices.label: D
choices.text: 24 to 48 hours

choices.label: E
choices.text: 60 to 70 days

explanation.summary: Disseminated T. solium larvae mature into cysticerci over about 60 to 70 days.
explanation.whyCorrect: In both humans and pigs, swallowed T. solium eggs hatch, invade the intestinal wall, enter the bloodstream, and migrate to tissue all over the body. The parasite then matures into cysticerci over the course of 60 to 70 days, and it is the presence of these cysts that drives the inflammation and tissue damage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Disease can surface years later, but cyst maturation itself is a matter of weeks to months.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A week is not enough time for the larvae to develop into mature cysticerci.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This overstates maturation time, although symptoms from the cysts may not appear for years.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This is far too short; maturation takes roughly two months, not a day or two.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man ate raw perch while on a fishing trip. Roughly how long after ingesting the plerocercoid will the worm reach adulthood and begin passing eggs in his stool?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 1 to 2 weeks

choices.label: B
choices.text: 3 months

choices.label: C
choices.text: 5 to 6 weeks

choices.label: D
choices.text: About 12 months

choices.label: E
choices.text: 24 to 48 hours

explanation.summary: A Diphyllobothrium plerocercoid takes about 5 to 6 weeks to reach adulthood and start shedding eggs.
explanation.whyCorrect: It takes roughly 5 to 6 weeks after infection for the plerocercoid to reach adulthood and begin passing eggs in a patient's stool. Stool examination done earlier than that can be negative even though the parasite is present.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Two weeks is still too early for the adult worm to begin shedding eggs.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Three months is the interval described for Taenia species, not for the fish tapeworm.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A year far overstates the interval; egg shedding begins about a month and a half after infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The plerocercoid needs weeks to grow into an egg-producing adult, not a day or two.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman swallows a cysticercus in undercooked beef. Which of the following best describes how long the worm takes to reach adulthood in her intestine and how long it can then survive?

choices.label: A
choices.text: About 2 days to mature, then survives several years

choices.label: B
choices.text: About 2 months to mature, then can survive for years

choices.label: C
choices.text: About 2 weeks to mature, then survives a few weeks

choices.label: D
choices.text: About 2 years to mature, then survives a few months

choices.label: E
choices.text: About 6 months to mature, then survives a few months

explanation.summary: In humans Taenia takes about 2 months to reach adulthood and can then live for years.
explanation.whyCorrect: In humans it takes about 2 months for Taenia species to reach adulthood, but the worm can live for years after infection. That long life span is why a carrier can shed eggs and gravid proglottids for a very long time, and it is also why most patients are diagnosed only when they notice passed segments.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Two days is far too fast for a cysticercus to become an egg-producing adult worm.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Two weeks is too short for maturation, and the adult worm survives far longer than a few weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Maturation takes about two months, not two years, and survival is measured in years.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Maturation is faster than this, and the worm can persist for years rather than months.

questions.stem: A medical student is comparing the adult worms of the tapeworms that infect humans. Which of the following statements about adult tapeworm size is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adult Diphyllobothrium worms can exceed 10 m in length

choices.label: B
choices.text: Adult Diphyllobothrium worms rarely exceed 1 m in length

choices.label: C
choices.text: Adult Taenia saginata worms never exceed 1 m in length

choices.label: D
choices.text: Adult Taenia solium worms are typically 10 to 20 m long

choices.label: E
choices.text: Adult Taenia solium worms carry fewer than 10 proglottids

explanation.summary: Diphyllobothrium is the world's largest tapeworm, with adults over 10 m and more than 3,000 proglottids.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adult Diphyllobothrium worms can reach lengths greater than 10 m, about 32.8 feet, and have more than 3,000 proglottids, which is why it is called the world's largest tapeworm. Despite that size, most patients have only moderate gastrointestinal symptoms or none at all.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The fish tapeworm routinely grows past 10 m, so a 1 m ceiling is the opposite of the truth.
whyWrongByChoice.C: T. saginata adults are usually 5 m or less and may reach as much as 25 m, far above 1 m.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Adult T. solium worms are 2 to 7 m long, well short of 10 to 20 m.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The body of a Taenia adult is made of many proglottids, not fewer than ten.

questions.stem: Two patients are seen in clinic, one with Taenia saginata and one with Taenia solium. Which of the following statements about the number of eggs produced per proglottid is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both species produce under 1,000 eggs per proglottid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Neither species exceeds 10,000 eggs per proglottid

choices.label: C
choices.text: T. saginata may produce up to 100,000 eggs per proglottid

choices.label: D
choices.text: T. solium may produce up to 500,000 eggs per proglottid

choices.label: E
choices.text: T. solium proglottids produce about twice as many eggs

explanation.summary: T. saginata may produce up to 100,000 eggs per proglottid, twice the output of T. solium.
explanation.whyCorrect: The adult worm produces proglottids, which together produce thousands of eggs a day. T. saginata may produce up to 100,000 eggs per proglottid and T. solium may produce 50,000. Those eggs survive for days to months in the environment, which is what keeps the cycle going through grazing livestock.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both species vastly exceed 1,000 eggs per proglottid.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Both species produce tens of thousands of eggs per proglottid, well above 10,000.
whyWrongByChoice.D: T. solium produces about 50,000 eggs per proglottid, not half a million.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The relationship is reversed; T. saginata produces roughly twice as many eggs per proglottid as T. solium.

questions.stem: Diphyllobothrium eggs passed in human feces reach fresh water, embryonate, and hatch. Which of the following is the next host in the life cycle of this parasite?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A domestic farm pig

choices.label: B
choices.text: A freshwater crustacean

choices.label: C
choices.text: A freshwater snail

choices.label: D
choices.text: A grazing beef cow

choices.label: E
choices.text: Another human being

explanation.summary: Hatched Diphyllobothrium larvae are taken up first by a freshwater crustacean, then by small fish, then by large fish.
explanation.whyCorrect: Once the eggs are passed they embryonate and hatch in water, and the parasite is then consumed by a freshwater crustacean, where it develops further. The crustacean is eaten by a small freshwater fish, which is eaten by a larger fish such as perch, salmon, or whitefish, and only in that large fish does the parasite reach the plerocercoid form infectious to humans.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pigs are the intermediate host for Taenia solium and Taenia asiatica.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The brick describes a crustacean followed by fish; snails play no part in this cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cattle are the intermediate host for Taenia saginata, not for the fish tapeworm.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Humans are infected only by eating plerocercoids in fish; swallowing the eggs does nothing.

questions.stem: A patient is found to be infected with a single adult Diphyllobothrium worm. Which of the following best describes the egg output of this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: About 1,000 eggs, released on a single occasion

choices.label: B
choices.text: About 6 eggs daily, matching its proglottid output

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fewer than 100 eggs over the entire life of the worm

choices.label: D
choices.text: No eggs, because it reproduces only inside the fish

choices.label: E
choices.text: Up to a million eggs passed in the stool per worm

explanation.summary: A single adult fish tapeworm can shed up to a million eggs in the stool.
explanation.whyCorrect: Eggs of Diphyllobothrium are passed in the feces, and up to a million eggs can be passed in the stool per worm. This enormous output is what keeps eggs reaching fresh water, where they embryonate and hatch to continue the cycle through crustaceans and fish.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Shedding is continuous while the adult worm lives, not a single release.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Six per day is the number of proglottids a Taenia adult sheds, not the egg output of this worm.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Egg output is enormous, on the order of a million rather than under a hundred.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The adult worm lives and reproduces in the human small intestine and sheds eggs in feces.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman with known taeniasis develops right upper quadrant pain, fever, and jaundice. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography shows a tapeworm segment lodged in the common bile duct. Which of the following complications has occurred?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Appendicitis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cholangitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lymphatic filariasis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Meningitis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neurocysticercosis

explanation.summary: A Taenia proglottid trapped in the bile ducts causes cholangitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most Taenia infections are asymptomatic or cause moderate gastrointestinal discomfort, and complications are rare. When they do occur, passed proglottids can get trapped in the appendix or in the bile ducts. A segment lodged in the bile duct produces cholangitis, inflammation of the bile ducts.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Appendicitis follows a proglottid trapped in the appendix, which would cause right lower quadrant pain.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lymphatic filariasis is caused by Wuchereria bancrofti and has nothing to do with tapeworm segments.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Meningitis in this brick is a feature of neurocysticercosis, not of a segment in the biliary tree.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neurocysticercosis requires larval cysts in the brain, not an adult worm segment in a duct.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man has had months of vague abdominal discomfort and has now passed a mass of worm segments after eating raw fish regularly for years. Which of the following complications is most consistent with this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Calcified cysts scattered in the brain and skeletal muscle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fulminant meningitis progressing over a few days

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gallbladder inflammation caused by passed proglottids

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lymphatic obstruction with swelling of the lower limbs

choices.label: E
choices.text: Seizures from inflammation around larval tissue cysts

explanation.summary: Diphyllobothriasis is usually mild, but passed proglottids can cause cholecystitis or cholangitis and the huge worm can rarely obstruct the bowel.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most patients with diphyllobothriasis have moderate gastrointestinal symptoms or none at all, because the worm contacts tissue only through its bothria and the immune system tolerates it well. Complications are rare but real: passed proglottids may cause cholecystitis, inflammation of the gallbladder, or cholangitis, and rarely the very large worm causes a bowel obstruction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Calcified tissue cysts are caused by Taenia solium; the fish tapeworm stays in the intestinal lumen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A rapidly progressive meningitis over days describes Naegleria fowleri, not a tapeworm.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lymphatic obstruction with limb swelling is caused by the filarial nematode Wuchereria bancrofti.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Seizures from tissue cysts are a feature of neurocysticercosis, which this parasite cannot cause.

questions.stem: A patient treated for diphyllobothriasis asks how to avoid becoming infected again without giving up fish entirely. Which of the following is the most appropriate advice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Avoid all contact with dogs, seals, and fish-eating birds

choices.label: B
choices.text: Avoid drinking untreated water from fresh lakes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Avoid eating undercooked pork and beef dishes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cook the fish thoroughly before eating it

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wash hands carefully after every use of the toilet

explanation.summary: Cooking fish destroys the plerocercoid, so properly cooked fish is safe.
explanation.whyCorrect: Humans acquire Diphyllobothrium by eating the plerocercoid in raw or undercooked fish, and cooking fish destroys the parasite. This is exactly the advice given to a patient who wants to keep eating fish, and it is the same reason menus warn that consuming raw or undercooked seafood raises the risk of foodborne illness.
