whyWrongByChoice.A: Dogs, seals, and birds are additional definitive hosts, but they do not transmit the parasite to people directly.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Infection comes from the flesh of large fish, not from drinking lake water.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pork and beef carry Taenia species, not the fish tapeworm.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Handwashing prevents fecal-oral spread of Taenia solium eggs; fish tapeworm eggs are not infectious to humans.

questions.stem: A restaurant cook is found to have an intestinal Taenia solium infection. Which of the following measures is most important to prevent cysticercosis among the people he serves?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cooking all fish served at the restaurant thoroughly

choices.label: B
choices.text: Keeping him off work until an antibody test turns negative

choices.label: C
choices.text: Removing all raw and undercooked beef dishes from the menu

choices.label: D
choices.text: Screening his customers with brain imaging for calcified cysts

choices.label: E
choices.text: Strict handwashing after defecation and before handling food

explanation.summary: Cysticercosis spreads fecal-orally from a tapeworm carrier's eggs, so handwashing and food hygiene are the key control.
explanation.whyCorrect: A person carrying an adult T. solium worm passes eggs in stool, and those eggs cause cysticercosis when other people swallow them. People consume feces in contaminated food handled by an infected food handler and from trace amounts on door handles, tables, and other frequently touched items, so proper hand washing and food handling is critical.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Thorough cooking of fish prevents diphyllobothriasis, an infection that never causes tissue cysts.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The antibody immunoassay cannot distinguish past from current infection, so it cannot clear him for work.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Beef transmits Taenia saginata, whose eggs do not hatch in humans and cannot cause cysticercosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Imaging detects disease that has already happened and prevents no transmission.

questions.stem: A veterinarian inspecting carcasses at a slaughterhouse finds cysticerci in the skeletal muscle of both cattle and pigs. Which of the following correctly pairs each animal with the tapeworm whose cysticerci it harbors?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both cattle and pigs harbor only Diphyllobothrium latum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both cattle and pigs harbor only T. saginata

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cattle harbor D. latum and pigs harbor T. saginata

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cattle harbor T. saginata and pigs harbor T. solium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cattle harbor T. solium and pigs harbor T. saginata

explanation.summary: T. saginata cycles through cattle, giving the beef tapeworm, while T. solium and T. asiatica cycle through pigs as pork tapeworms.
explanation.whyCorrect: T. saginata infects cows, hence the nickname beef tapeworm, while T. solium and T. asiatica infect pigs and are called pork tapeworms. Livestock become infected by ingesting vegetation contaminated with human eggs or gravid proglottids; the eggs hatch, the cestode penetrates the intestinal wall and disseminates through the body, and cysticerci form in the muscles.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Diphyllobothrium cycles through freshwater crustaceans and fish, never through livestock.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pigs carry T. solium and T. asiatica, not T. saginata.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neither pairing is right: the fish tapeworm does not use cattle, and pigs do not carry the beef tapeworm.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The pairing is reversed; the pork tapeworm belongs to pigs and the beef tapeworm to cattle.

questions.stem: A laboratory technician accidentally swallows a small amount of a stool specimen that contains Diphyllobothrium eggs. Which of the following is the most likely outcome?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An adult worm will mature in her gut in 5 to 6 weeks

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cysts will form in her brain and muscle over about 2 months

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nothing will happen, as the eggs cannot infect humans

choices.label: D
choices.text: Plerocercoid larvae will develop within her skeletal muscle

choices.label: E
choices.text: The eggs will hatch and the larvae will invade her liver

explanation.summary: Diphyllobothrium eggs are harmless to humans; only the plerocercoid in fish is infectious.
explanation.whyCorrect: If humans consume the eggs passed in feces, nothing happens. The life cycle requires the eggs to leave the human host, embryonate and hatch in water, pass through a freshwater crustacean and then small fish, and reach the plerocercoid stage in a large fish before they can infect a person again.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An adult worm develops only after a person eats a plerocercoid in fish, not after swallowing eggs.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Tissue cysts after swallowing eggs are unique to Taenia solium, not to the fish tapeworm.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Plerocercoids develop in fish; they never form in human muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This parasite does not invade human tissue at any stage of its life cycle.

questions.stem: Apart from humans, which of the following can also serve as a definitive host for Diphyllobothrium species?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cattle and pigs that graze on contaminated pasture

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fish-eating mammals and birds, such as dogs and seals

choices.label: C
choices.text: Freshwater crustaceans that ingest the hatched larvae

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mosquitoes that transmit larvae during a blood meal

choices.label: E
choices.text: Small freshwater fish that carry procercoid larvae

explanation.summary: Other fish-eating mammals and birds are definitive hosts too, so the parasite does not need humans.
explanation.whyCorrect: Humans are a definitive host for Diphyllobothrium spp., but other fish-eating mammals such as dogs and seals, and birds, can also serve as definitive hosts. Because the adult worm can mature in these animals, the parasite does not need humans to complete its life cycle.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cattle and pigs are intermediate hosts for Taenia species, not hosts for the fish tapeworm.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The crustacean is the first intermediate host, where a larval stage develops rather than an adult worm.
whyWrongByChoice.D: There is no arthropod vector in this life cycle; transmission is by eating infected fish.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Small fish are intermediate hosts that pass the larva along to larger predator fish.

questions.stem: In some developing countries, neurocysticercosis is reported to be the single most common cause of which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adult-onset seizures

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chronic diarrhea in adult patients

choices.label: C
choices.text: Febrile illness in young children

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lymphatic obstruction

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vitamin B12 deficiency

explanation.summary: Seizures are the most common presentation of neurocysticercosis, and in some developing countries it is the leading cause of adult-onset seizures.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cysts in the brain and the inflammation around them leave calcified lesions and irritate cortical tissue. Seizures are the most common clinical presentation of neurocysticercosis, and in some developing countries neurocysticercosis is the most common cause of adult-onset seizures. Altered vision, focal neurologic signs, and meningitis are other recognized presentations.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Intestinal tapeworm infection causes mild gastrointestinal symptoms, not a leading cause of chronic diarrhea.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This brick does not associate neurocysticercosis with childhood febrile illness.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lymphatic obstruction is caused by Wuchereria bancrofti, which causes lymphatic filariasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Low vitamin B12 is the finding associated with the fish tapeworm, not with brain cysts.

questions.stem: Which of the following organisms can form cysts throughout the body, including in the brain, after a person swallows its eggs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diphyllobothrium latum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Taenia asiatica

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taenia saginata

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taenia solium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wuchereria bancrofti

explanation.summary: Only Taenia solium causes cysticercosis, because only its eggs hatch inside a human.
explanation.whyCorrect: Only T. solium can cause cysticercosis. Its eggs hatch when swallowed by humans, and the larvae invade the intestinal wall, enter the bloodstream, and form cysts throughout the body. Most end up in muscle, but those that reach the brain cause neurocysticercosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Swallowed fish tapeworm eggs do nothing in humans; the worm stays in the gut lumen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Like T. saginata, this species causes intestinal infection only and never tissue cysts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Its eggs do not hatch in humans, so swallowing them causes no tissue infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This nematode causes lymphatic filariasis and does not form cysts in tissue.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man who emigrated 32 years ago and has never returned develops new-onset seizures. CT of the head shows several calcified intracranial lesions. The consulting team doubts a parasitic cause because his exposure would have been so long ago. Which of the following best addresses their concern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An adult worm migrated from the intestine into the brain

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antibody testing would have reverted to negative by now

choices.label: C
choices.text: Calcified brain lesions are not caused by any tapeworm

choices.label: D
choices.text: He must have been reinfected by eating undercooked pork

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neurocysticercosis can appear more than 30 years later

explanation.summary: Neurocysticercosis can surface decades after the initial infection, with documented cases more than 30 years out.
explanation.whyCorrect: Neurocysticercosis can present years after the initial infection as cysts and the inflammation around them leave calcified lesions in the brain. In rare instances, neurologic infections have been documented more than 30 years after the initial infection, so a remote exposure history does not exclude the diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The adult worm stays attached in the intestine; it is the hatched larva that migrates through the bloodstream.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The immunoassay cannot distinguish past from current infection, so it may still be positive after many years.
whyWrongByChoice.C: T. solium cysticerci in the brain calcify and are a well-described cause of these lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Eating cysticerci in pork produces an intestinal adult worm, not brain cysts.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old man being evaluated for neurocysticercosis also undergoes radiographs of the thighs, which show numerous small calcified densities within the muscles of both legs. Which of the following best explains this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A coexisting fish tapeworm that invaded the leg muscles

choices.label: B
choices.text: Calcified adult worms that migrated out of the intestine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cysticerci that lodged in the muscles and later calcified

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lymphatic obstruction from a filarial nematode infection

choices.label: E
choices.text: Plerocercoid larvae that encysted after he ate raw fish

explanation.summary: Disseminated T. solium larvae seed muscle as well as brain, and those muscle cysts can calcify and show on imaging.
explanation.whyCorrect: When T. solium eggs hatch in a human, the larvae spread through the bloodstream to tissue all over the body. Most end up in muscle, where the cysts cause little trouble and often go unnoticed, while those reaching the central nervous system cause the neurologic disease. Calcified cysts in the legs can therefore be seen alongside neurocysticercosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The fish tapeworm stays in the lumen of the small intestine and never invades muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Adult tapeworms remain attached in the intestine; only the hatched larvae disseminate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lymphatic filariasis from Wuchereria bancrofti causes lymphatic obstruction, not calcified muscle nodules.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Plerocercoids develop in fish tissue, not in human muscle.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man returns from three months of agricultural work in rural Southeast Asia, where he often worked barefoot in wet fields. He first noticed an itchy rash on his feet, then developed a dry cough, and now has intermittent diarrhea and abdominal pain. Stool microscopy reveals motile rhabditiform larvae. Which of the following best describes how this organism entered his body?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct penetration of intact skin by filariform larvae in soil

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ingestion of embryonated eggs in contaminated drinking water

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ingestion of undercooked freshwater fish containing larvae

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ingestion of undercooked pork containing encysted larvae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhalation of aerosolized larvae from dried contaminated dust

explanation.summary: Strongyloides stercoralis is a soil-transmitted nematode whose filariform larvae burrow directly through intact skin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Strongyloides spp., Ancylostoma spp., and Necator americanus are the soil-transmitted helminths: they are acquired when a person walks on soil contaminated with the parasite. Unlike the tapeworms acquired by eating undercooked meat, these roundworms do not have to be consumed at all — the filariform larval stage in soil burrows directly into the skin of the definitive host. Barefoot contact with warm, wet soil in a tropical region is the classic exposure.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Fecal-oral ingestion of embryonated eggs is the route for Ascaris spp., which cannot burrow through skin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Undercooked freshwater fish transmits the fish tapeworm, not a skin-penetrating roundworm.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ingestion of larvae encysted in undercooked meat describes the tapeworms, not a soil-transmitted nematode.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Helminths in this group are not transmitted by inhaled aerosols or respiratory droplets.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old woman who emigrated from a rural tropical region 12 years ago reports recurrent, intensely itchy linear red tracks over her buttocks and thighs; individual tracks appear and fade within hours. Stool examination reveals rhabditiform larvae of Strongyloides stercoralis. Which of the following terms best describes her rash?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cutaneous larva migrans

choices.label: B
choices.text: Erythema marginatum

choices.label: C
choices.text: Erythema migrans

choices.label: D
choices.text: Erythema nodosum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Larva currens

explanation.summary: The migrating, pruritic, linear rash caused by Strongyloides larvae burrowing through skin is called larva currens.
explanation.whyCorrect: When filariform larvae penetrate skin and wiggle through it searching for a blood vessel or lymphatic, they leave a mild, pruritic, erythematous, linear rash named larva currens. In chronic strongyloidiasis the same appearance recurs on the buttocks, perineum, and thighs because autoinfective filariform larvae burrow out of the perianal region and back into the skin there.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cutaneous larva migrans is the name given to the rash of Ancylostoma/Necator spp., not to the Strongyloides rash.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Erythema marginatum is a non-pruritic, evanescent ring-shaped rash unrelated to helminth migration.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Erythema migrans is the expanding target-like rash of a tick-borne bacterial infection, not a larval track.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Erythema nodosum consists of tender subcutaneous nodules on the shins, not migrating linear tracks.

questions.stem: A patient becomes infected with Strongyloides stercoralis after walking barefoot on contaminated soil. Which of the following sequences best describes the infectious cycle of this parasite within the host?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ingestion of eggs, blood vessels, lungs, coughed up and swallowed, colon and cecum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ingestion of eggs, small intestine, colon, perianal skin, environment, reingestion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Skin penetration, blood vessels or lymphatics, lungs, coughed up and swallowed, small intestine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Skin penetration, lymph nodes, liver, portal circulation, small intestine, colon

choices.label: E
choices.text: Skin penetration, subcutaneous tissue only, spontaneous death of larvae after weeks

explanation.summary: Strongyloides filariform larvae go skin to bloodstream or lymphatics to lungs, then are coughed up, swallowed, and mature in the small intestine.
explanation.whyCorrect: The filariform larva penetrates skin and burrows until it finds a blood vessel or lymphatic. It is carried to the lungs, where it matures further, then is coughed up and swallowed. Once in the small intestine the larva matures into an adult female, which embeds in the submucosa. This skin-blood-lung-gut route is shared with the hookworms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ingestion of eggs with a lung migration describes Ascaris spp., and those adults live in the small intestine, not the cecum.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Egg ingestion followed by colonic maturation and perianal egg laying describes the pinworm cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.D: There is no hepatic or portal phase in the Strongyloides cycle; larvae reach the lungs from the systemic circulation or lymphatics.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Larvae dying in the skin without reaching the circulation describes Ancylostoma braziliense, not S. stercoralis.

questions.stem: An adult Strongyloides stercoralis worm is recovered from the duodenal mucosa of an infected patient. Which of the following is most likely true of this worm and how it reproduces inside the host?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both male and female worms are present and reproduce sexually in the mucosa

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a female worm that produces fertilized eggs asexually in the submucosa

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is a female worm whose eggs are fertilized by males arriving from the lungs

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a hermaphroditic worm that self-fertilizes within the intestinal lumen

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is a male worm that fertilizes females embedded in the duodenal mucosa

explanation.summary: Only female Strongyloides adults parasitize humans, and they produce fertilized eggs asexually in the intestinal submucosa.
explanation.whyCorrect: Larvae that reach the small intestine mature into adult females; males do not cause infection. The female embeds in the submucosa of the small intestine and asexually produces fertilized eggs, which hatch in the mucosa to release rhabditiform larvae. Males and females do meet and reproduce sexually, but only outside the host, in the free-living soil cycle.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both sexes mating in the intestine describes hookworms, which is precisely what distinguishes them from Strongyloides spp.
whyWrongByChoice.C: No male worms migrate from the lungs; the parasitic adult population in humans is female only.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The brick describes asexual production of fertilized eggs by the female, not hermaphroditic self-fertilization.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Male Strongyloides worms do not establish infection in humans and are not found parasitizing the gut.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man has had mild intermittent abdominal discomfort for 20 years. He immigrated from a tropical country two decades ago and has not traveled since. Stool studies now reveal Strongyloides stercoralis larvae. Which feature of this parasite best explains an infection persisting for 20 years without re-exposure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adult worms are continually reacquired from household contacts by fomites

choices.label: B
choices.text: Adult worms survive in the small intestine for decades without laying eggs

choices.label: C
choices.text: Eggs lie dormant in the biliary tree and hatch intermittently over decades

choices.label: D
choices.text: Encysted larvae in skeletal muscle periodically release progeny into the blood

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rhabditiform larvae mature to filariform larvae and reinvade gut or perianal skin

explanation.summary: Autoinfection lets Strongyloides complete its entire cycle inside one host, so infection is lifelong without treatment.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rhabditiform larvae hatching in the intestinal mucosa do not have to leave the body. Some mature into filariform larvae that burrow back through the intestinal mucosa or through the perianal skin, find a blood vessel, and restart the lung-to-gut migration. This autoinfective loop means a person infected with Strongyloides spp. stays infected for life unless anti-parasitics are given.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Person-to-person fomite spread characterizes pinworm eggs, not Strongyloides filariform larvae.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Persistence depends on continuous reinfection of the host, not on unusually long-lived, non-reproducing adults.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Strongyloides eggs hatch in the intestinal mucosa; they do not lie dormant in the biliary tree.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Encystment in skeletal muscle is not part of the Strongyloides life cycle described in this brick.

questions.stem: Rhabditiform larvae of Strongyloides stercoralis are passed in the stool of an infected patient and reach warm, moist soil. In addition to developing into infective filariform larvae, which of the following can these larvae do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Develop into adults capable of reproducing only inside a canine host

choices.label: B
choices.text: Develop into male and female adults that reproduce within the soil

choices.label: C
choices.text: Embryonate over roughly 18 days before becoming able to infect skin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Encyst within soil particles and remain infective for several decades

choices.label: E
choices.text: Enter a snail intermediate host before becoming able to infect humans

explanation.summary: Strongyloides has a free-living cycle in which soil-dwelling adults reproduce sexually outside any host.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rhabditiform larvae passed in the stool have two options. They can develop directly into filariform larvae that penetrate the next host's skin, or they can develop into male and female adults that reproduce sexually in the soil. That second option is the free-living cycle, in which adult worms can go on reproducing outside a host indefinitely.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dogs can serve as definitive hosts, but free-living soil reproduction needs no host at all.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A required embryonation period in soil applies to Ascaris eggs, not to larvae that have already hatched.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Strongyloides larvae do not encyst in soil; they either develop to filariform larvae or become free-living adults.
whyWrongByChoice.E: No snail or other intermediate host is required for any stage of the Strongyloides life cycle.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man who immigrated from Southeast Asia is started on high-dose prednisone for a newly diagnosed autoimmune disease. Three weeks later he develops severe abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea, hemoptysis, and gram-negative sepsis; chest radiograph shows diffuse interstitial infiltrates. Which of the following best explains his deterioration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A hypersensitivity reaction to dying worms triggered by the corticosteroid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Acquisition of a new soil-transmitted infection while he was hospitalized

choices.label: C
choices.text: Direct corticosteroid toxicity to gut mucosa allowing worms to invade

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of immune control over autoinfection causing hyperinfection syndrome

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reactivation of larvae encysted in his skeletal muscle by the corticosteroid

explanation.summary: Severe immunosuppression, especially high-dose corticosteroids, converts chronic strongyloidiasis into hyperinfection syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: In chronic strongyloidiasis the immune system holds the autoinfective cycle in check. Severe immunosuppression or high-dose corticosteroid treatment lets the autoinfection cycle accelerate, and the parasite burden explodes. Burrowing larvae disseminate beyond the gastrointestinal tract and lungs, producing GI bleeding and obstruction, pneumonitis with hemoptysis and diffuse infiltrates, meningitis, and sepsis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The syndrome is driven by an enormous live parasite burden, not by an allergic response to dying worms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A newly acquired soil-transmitted infection could not produce disseminated disease within three weeks in a hospital.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Larvae penetrate intestinal mucosa as a normal part of autoinfection, independent of steroid mucosal toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Strongyloides does not encyst in skeletal muscle; the reservoir is the ongoing autoinfective cycle itself.

questions.stem: A patient with chronic strongyloidiasis develops hyperinfection syndrome with dissemination of larvae beyond the gastrointestinal tract and lungs. Even with appropriate anti-parasitic treatment, which of the following best approximates the mortality of this condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Approximately 10 percent

choices.label: B
choices.text: Approximately 25 percent

choices.label: C
choices.text: Approximately 50 percent

choices.label: D
choices.text: Approximately 90 percent

choices.label: E
choices.text: Less than 1 percent

explanation.summary: Mortality of Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome with dissemination approaches 90 percent even when treated.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although most Strongyloides infections are mild or asymptomatic, hyperinfection with dissemination is a catastrophic illness. Larvae spread throughout the body causing GI hemorrhage and obstruction, pneumonitis, meningitis, and sepsis. Mortality is near 90 percent even with treatment, which is why identifying and treating chronic infection before immunosuppression matters so much.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A 10 percent figure would describe a serious but usually survivable illness, which this is not.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A one-in-four mortality is far lower than what disseminated strongyloidiasis carries.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This substantially understates the lethality of disseminated hyperinfection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Under 1 percent describes uncomplicated chronic strongyloidiasis, not hyperinfection with dissemination.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old asymptomatic woman from a strongyloidiasis-endemic region is evaluated before starting immunosuppressive therapy. Which of the following laboratory findings is present in roughly three-quarters of patients with chronic strongyloidiasis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elevated IgE or a mild eosinophilia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Elevated serum IgA with thrombocytosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Elevated serum IgM with lymphopenia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Microcytic anemia with a low ferritin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neutrophilia with a marked left shift

explanation.summary: Roughly 75 percent of patients with chronic strongyloidiasis have an elevated IgE or a mild eosinophilia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic strongyloidiasis is usually asymptomatic, so laboratory clues carry weight. About 75 percent of chronically infected patients show either an elevated IgE or mild eosinophilia, the expected type 2 immune signature of a persistent tissue-migrating helminth. These findings should prompt evaluation before starting corticosteroids or other immunosuppression.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Elevated IgA with thrombocytosis is not associated with this infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Elevated IgM with lymphopenia is not a described feature of chronic strongyloidiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Microcytic anemia with low ferritin points to blood-feeding hookworms, not to Strongyloides.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neutrophilia with a left shift suggests acute bacterial infection rather than a chronic helminth infection.

questions.stem: A clinician suspects chronic strongyloidiasis in a patient with years of intermittent diarrhea and a recurring migratory pruritic rash. Which of the following findings on specialized stool examination is the most common way this diagnosis is established?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mammillated eggs with rounded bumps over the outer shell

choices.label: B
choices.text: Motile rhabditiform larvae, or occasionally a passed adult

choices.label: C
choices.text: Proglottid segments containing branched uterine structures

choices.label: D
choices.text: Smooth-shelled eggs whose interior contains multiple nodules

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transparent elongated eggs that are flat along one side

explanation.summary: Strongyloidiasis is diagnosed by seeing rhabditiform larvae in stool, because the eggs hatch before they are passed.
explanation.whyCorrect: Specialized stool examination is the gold standard for strongyloidiasis. Because eggs hatch within the intestinal mucosa, what appears in stool is the rhabditiform larva, not an egg. Visualizing those larvae, or occasionally a passed adult, is the most common way the diagnosis is made. Parasite burden is low in chronic infection, so repeated samples are needed to approach full sensitivity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mammillated bumpy eggs are the unfertilized eggs of Ascaris spp.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Proglottid segments come from tapeworms, which are cestodes rather than nematodes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Smooth-shelled eggs with internal nodules are the eggs of Ancylostoma/Necator spp.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transparent elongated eggs flattened on one side are those of Enterobius vermicularis.

questions.stem: A patient with a high clinical suspicion for strongyloidiasis has had three separate specialized stool examinations, all negative for larvae. Which of the following is the best next step to increase diagnostic sensitivity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bronchoalveolar lavage, the preferred test in uncomplicated disease

choices.label: B
choices.text: Colonoscopy, which reliably visualizes the adult worms in the gut

choices.label: C
choices.text: Duodenal aspiration, which is more sensitive than stool examination

choices.label: D
choices.text: Peripheral blood smear, which shows circulating filariform larvae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serologic testing, which is highly specific for Strongyloides spp.

explanation.summary: When stool studies are repeatedly negative, duodenal aspiration is the more sensitive, though more invasive, option.
explanation.whyCorrect: Parasite burden in chronic strongyloidiasis is low, so stool examinations are often falsely negative and must be repeated. Duodenal aspirates are more invasive than stool collection but have a higher sensitivity, sampling the site where the adult females are embedded and the larvae hatch. It is therefore the appropriate escalation after repeatedly negative stools.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bronchoalveolar lavage is invasive and reserved for hyperinfection when sputum is inadequate, not for uncomplicated disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Strongyloides adults are only 1 to 6 mm long and are not sought by colonoscopy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Strongyloides larvae are not identified by examining a peripheral blood smear.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serology is available but cross-reacts with other parasitic species, so its usefulness is limited.

questions.stem: A critically ill patient with Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome has diffuse pulmonary infiltrates, but repeated sputum samples are inadequate for analysis. Which of the following procedures is most appropriate to recover the parasite from the lungs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bronchoalveolar lavage with instilled and aspirated saline

choices.label: B
choices.text: Open surgical lung biopsy with frozen-section examination

choices.label: C
choices.text: Percutaneous transthoracic needle aspiration of an infiltrate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Repeat induced sputum after nebulized hypertonic saline

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thoracentesis with microscopic examination of pleural fluid

explanation.summary: In hyperinfection, bronchoalveolar lavage can recover larvae from the lungs when sputum is inadequate.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bronchoalveolar lavage is a minimally invasive procedure in which sterile saline is instilled into the lungs and aspirated back. Because hyperinfection sends larvae into the pulmonary tissue, sampling lung fluid this way can reveal the parasite. It is specifically useful when sputum does not provide a good sample, and because it is invasive it is reserved for exactly this situation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Open lung biopsy is far more invasive than needed when lavage can sample the same compartment.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Needle aspiration of an infiltrate carries added risk and is not the described approach for recovering larvae.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sputum sampling has already failed in this patient, which is the stated indication to move to lavage.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The larvae disperse into lung tissue and airways, so pleural fluid is not the appropriate specimen.

questions.stem: A public health trainee reviews the global burden of Strongyloides stercoralis. Which of the following best characterizes the epidemiology of strongyloidiasis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: About 2 billion people, distributed evenly across all world climates

choices.label: B
choices.text: About 5 million people, concentrated in temperate northern Europe

choices.label: C
choices.text: About 50 million people, almost entirely within the United States

choices.label: D
choices.text: About 613 million people, concentrated in arid desert environments

choices.label: E
choices.text: About 613 million people, mostly in tropical and subtropical regions

explanation.summary: Strongyloidiasis affects an estimated 613 million people, concentrated in tropical and subtropical regions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Strongyloides spp. are distributed through tropical and subtropical areas worldwide, with transmission usually occurring in summer months. An estimated 613 million people globally have strongyloidiasis, and South-East Asia, Africa, and the Western Pacific account for most cases. Disease burden clusters where sanitation is poor and in rural, remote, and socially marginalized communities.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Two billion overstates the figure, and the distribution is climate-dependent rather than uniform.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The burden is far larger than 5 million and is not centered in temperate northern Europe.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Strongyloidiasis is uncommon in the United States, seen mainly in travelers and immigrants.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The parasite requires warm, moist soil; arid deserts are not where cases concentrate.

questions.stem: Scanning electron microscopy of the anterior end of Ancylostoma duodenale demonstrates prominent tooth-like hooks, while the corresponding view of Necator americanus shows cutting plates. What is the primary function of these structures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To anchor the worm to the lining of the intestine

choices.label: B
choices.text: To attach to the alveolar wall during migration through the lungs

choices.label: C
choices.text: To bore through the skin at the site of initial larval entry

choices.label: D
choices.text: To crush and break open ingested host red blood cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: To rasp off and ingest intestinal epithelial cells for nutrition

explanation.summary: Hookworms are named for mouthparts whose hooks or plates anchor the adult worm to the intestinal lining.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ancylostoma duodenale, A. ceylanicum, and Necator americanus are collectively called hookworms because of their mouths. The special hooks or plates at the anterior end are used to anchor the worm to the lining of the intestines, which is how the adults hold position in the jejunum while feeding on host blood.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Larvae pass through the lungs transiently and are coughed up; they do not anchor to alveoli.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Skin entry is accomplished by the filariform larval stage, which does not yet have these adult mouthparts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Red cells are not mechanically crushed by the mouthparts; the structures serve attachment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The adults feed on host blood at the attachment site rather than rasping and eating epithelial cells.

questions.stem: A global health agency is mapping hookworm infection worldwide. Which of the following best describes the burden and geographic distribution of Ancylostoma/Necator infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: About 1.2 billion people, found most commonly in the southern United States

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fewer than 10 million people, confined to high-altitude mountainous regions

choices.label: C
choices.text: About 613 million people, found almost exclusively in the Western Pacific

choices.label: D
choices.text: Over 700 million people, concentrated in cold and dry temperate climates

choices.label: E
choices.text: Over 700 million people, most abundant in warm and moist equatorial regions

explanation.summary: Hookworms infect over 700 million people and are most abundant in warm, moist areas near the equator.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hookworms have a worldwide distribution but thrive where soil is warm and moist, so countries near the equator carry the highest risk. Africa, Southeast Asia, Latin America, the Middle East, the Caribbean, and rarely the southern United States are the regions involved. Globally, hookworm infections affect over 700 million people.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 1.2 billion is the upper estimate for ascariasis, and the southern United States is only a rare site.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The burden is enormous, and cold high-altitude soil does not support the free-living larval stage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 613 million is the figure quoted for strongyloidiasis, and hookworms are not restricted to one region.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The number is right, but cold, dry climates are the opposite of the conditions hookworms require.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man develops an extremely itchy, raised, serpiginous track on his foot several days after walking barefoot on a Caribbean beach. Weeks later, stool microscopy shows oval eggs with a smooth outer shell and multiple nodules within. Which of the following terms best describes his initial skin finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Allergic contact dermatitis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cutaneous larva migrans

choices.label: C
choices.text: Erythema chronicum migrans

choices.label: D
choices.text: Larva currens

choices.label: E
choices.text: Necrotizing soft tissue infection

explanation.summary: The intensely pruritic serpiginous rash produced by Ancylostoma/Necator larvae entering skin is called cutaneous larva migrans.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hookworm filariform larvae penetrate healthy skin from contaminated soil and sand, producing a rash similar in appearance to that of Strongyloides. The brick names this initial hookworm rash cutaneous larva migrans, describing it as extremely itchy and often serpiginous. The smooth-shelled eggs with internal nodules found later in stool confirm an Ancylostoma/Necator infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Allergic contact dermatitis follows the distribution of a contactant and does not migrate as a track.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Erythema chronicum migrans is a bacterial tick-borne rash with no larval migration.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Larva currens is the term reserved for the migrating rash of Strongyloides spp.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Necrotizing soft tissue infection is a rapidly progressive bacterial process, not a pruritic track.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman who has not traveled outside the United States in eight years is found to have hookworm eggs in her stool during an evaluation for iron deficiency. She spent her childhood in rural West Africa. Which property of Ancylostoma spp. best explains this presentation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adult worms survive and lay eggs in the intestine for more than 30 years

choices.label: B
choices.text: Eggs hatch within the human intestine and restart the cycle internally

choices.label: C
choices.text: Larvae lie dormant in host tissue and reactivate years after exposure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Larvae persist in the soil around the patient's home for many years

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rhabditiform larvae reinvade the intestinal mucosa, causing autoinfection

explanation.summary: Hookworm larvae can become developmentally arrested in host tissue and reactivate years after the original exposure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ancylostoma larvae that penetrate the skin may become dormant within host tissues rather than completing migration. These arrested larvae can reactivate years later, enter the small intestine, and mature into egg-laying adults. As a result, a hookworm infection may only become clinically evident long after the person has left the endemic area.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adult hookworms live roughly 1 to 5 years, far short of three decades.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hookworm eggs do not hatch in humans; they must be passed in stool and hatch in soil.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Soil larvae near her home would require new skin exposure and would not explain an old African exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hookworms cannot autoinfect; that mechanism is specific to Strongyloides spp.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old boy in rural Latin America has fatigue and pallor, with a hemoglobin of 7.8 g/dL and a low serum ferritin. Stool microscopy reveals hookworm eggs. Which of the following best explains his anemia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adult worms anchored in the small intestine feed on host blood

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autoantibodies induced by the worms destroy circulating red cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Migrating larvae cause chronic hemorrhage within the alveoli

choices.label: D
choices.text: The worms competitively absorb dietary vitamin B12 in the ileum

choices.label: E
choices.text: The worms secrete a toxin that suppresses marrow erythropoiesis

explanation.summary: Adult hookworms take a blood meal from the intestinal wall, and a heavy burden causes iron-deficiency anemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adult hookworms anchor in the jejunum and feed on the blood of the host. In a light infection the loss is minimal, but with a high worm burden the cumulative blood loss produces iron deficiency anemia, reflected here in the low ferritin and microcytic picture. In children this chronic loss can also cause growth restriction. Visible blood in the stool is possible but rare.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hookworms do not cause an autoimmune hemolytic anemia, and hemolysis would not lower ferritin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The pulmonary phase is brief and does not cause the ongoing blood loss needed for iron deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Competition for vitamin B12 causes a macrocytic anemia and is a feature of a fish tapeworm, not hookworm.
whyWrongByChoice.E: No marrow-suppressing toxin is described; the anemia is from external blood loss into the gut.

questions.stem: A parasitologist compares adult worms recovered from the small intestine of a patient with hookworm infection with those from a patient with strongyloidiasis. Which of the following findings is expected in the hookworm case but not in the strongyloidiasis case?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both male and female adults are present and mate within the gut

choices.label: B
choices.text: Only female adult worms are recovered from the intestinal lumen

choices.label: C
choices.text: The adult worms are embedded within the intestinal submucosa

choices.label: D
choices.text: The adult worms measure between 1 and 6 mm in total length

choices.label: E
choices.text: The adult worms produce fertilized eggs without ever mating

explanation.summary: Hookworms have both sexes in the human intestine and reproduce sexually there, unlike the female-only Strongyloides.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both male and female hookworms are present in the intestines, where sexual reproduction occurs and fertilized eggs are then passed in the feces. This is explicitly distinct from Strongyloides spp., in which only females are found in the intestines and produce eggs asexually. It is one of the cleanest contrasts between the two skin-penetrating groups.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A female-only intestinal population is precisely what characterizes strongyloidiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Embedding in the submucosa describes the Strongyloides female, not the attached hookworm adult.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 1 to 6 mm is the size given for Strongyloides adults; hookworm adults are about 1 cm.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Asexual production of fertilized eggs is the Strongyloides pattern, the opposite of hookworm biology.

questions.stem: A patient treated for hookworm infection is counseled that, unlike strongyloidiasis, this infection will not persist indefinitely in the absence of renewed exposure to contaminated soil. Which of the following facts best supports that counseling?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hookworm adults are cleared by the host immune response within weeks

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hookworm adults migrate out of the body through the perianal skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hookworm eggs are destroyed by gastric acid before reaching the colon

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hookworm eggs cannot hatch in humans and must hatch in the soil

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hookworm larvae are unable to penetrate intact skin a second time

explanation.summary: Hookworms cannot autoinfect because their eggs must be passed in stool and hatch in soil before infecting anyone.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ancylostoma/Necator spp. cannot cause autoinfection. Their eggs do not hatch inside humans; they must be passed in the stool, hatch in soil, and develop through rhabditiform to filariform larvae there before another infection can occur. This is a key distinction from Strongyloides, whose larvae hatch in the gut mucosa and can reinvade the same host.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adult hookworms actually survive 1 to 5 years in an untreated host, so immune clearance is not the reason.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Perianal emergence describes the gravid pinworm female, not hookworm adults.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The limitation is that eggs require the external environment, not that acid destroys them in transit.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Filariform larvae can penetrate the skin of a previously infected person; reinfection from soil is possible.

questions.stem: In an untreated host, adult Ancylostoma/Necator worms residing in the small intestine are characterized by which of the following combinations of egg output and lifespan?

choices.label: A
choices.text: About 200 eggs per female per day, with a lifespan of about 2 months

choices.label: B
choices.text: About 2,000 eggs per female per day, with a lifespan of up to 30 years

choices.label: C
choices.text: About 20,000 eggs per female per day, with a lifespan of 1 to 5 years

choices.label: D
choices.text: About 20,000 eggs per female per day, with a lifespan of 2 to 3 weeks

choices.label: E
choices.text: About 200,000 eggs per female per day, with a lifespan of 1 to 5 years

explanation.summary: Adult hookworms live 1 to 5 years, and each female sheds about 20,000 eggs per day.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adult hookworms persist for several years in the small intestine, typically 1 to 5 years, and each female produces roughly 20,000 eggs a day. That sustained output is what keeps environmental contamination high in endemic areas, and the multi-year lifespan, combined with larval dormancy in tissue, explains why infections can stay evident long after exposure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This output is far too low, and a 2-month lifespan is the figure given for adult pinworms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Neither the egg count nor a 30-year lifespan matches hookworm biology.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The egg number is right but the lifespan is years, not a few weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 200,000 eggs per day is the output described for an Ascaris female, not a hookworm.

questions.stem: Two weeks after a barefoot hike through a warm, muddy area, a 32-year-old woman develops a persistent cough, wheezing, and chest pain. Chest radiograph shows patchy infiltrates resembling a bronchopneumonia, and her blood eosinophil count is elevated. Which of the following best explains her pulmonary findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adult hookworms lodging within and obstructing the small bronchioles

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bacterial superinfection seeded from hookworms within the intestine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Direct cytotoxic injury from hookworms attaching to the alveolar wall

choices.label: D
choices.text: Eosinophils recruited to the lung degranulating around migrating larvae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hookworm eggs embolizing into the pulmonary capillary circulation

explanation.summary: Eosinophilic pneumonitis in hookworm infection results from eosinophils degranulating around larvae migrating through the lungs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although the pulmonary phase of Ancylostoma/Necator infection is usually mild or asymptomatic, eosinophilic pneumonitis occurs rarely. Eosinophils are recruited to the lungs and degranulate, releasing mediators intended to kill the migrating larvae. The result is a persistent cough, wheezing, chest pain, and rarely hemoptysis, with a chest radiograph that can mimic bronchopneumonia and is indistinct from other etiologies.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Only larvae transit the lungs; the adult worms reside in the small intestine, not the airways.
whyWrongByChoice.B: There is no described bacterial seeding of the lungs from intestinal hookworms.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hookworms attach to the intestinal lining, not to alveolar walls; the lung injury is immune-mediated.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hookworm eggs are passed in feces and do not embolize to the pulmonary vasculature.

questions.stem: Microscopic examination of respiratory secretions from a patient with pulmonary symptoms during a helminth infection reveals slender, pointed, needle-shaped crystals. These crystals are composed primarily of which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Calcium oxalate precipitated from serum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Galectin-10 derived from eosinophils

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immunoglobulin E from local plasma cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Myeloperoxidase derived from neutrophils

choices.label: E
choices.text: Surfactant protein from type II pneumocytes

explanation.summary: Charcot-Leyden crystals are made of eosinophil proteins, mostly galectin-10.
explanation.whyCorrect: Eosinophilic reactions in the lungs can generate small, microscopic, needle-like crystals called Charcot-Leyden crystals. They are composed of eosinophil proteins, mostly galectin-10, and form during either allergic reactions or parasitic infections, so finding them points to those two categories. Importantly, they do not always form, so their absence does not rule out either process.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Calcium oxalate crystals are a urinary and renal finding, unrelated to eosinophilic lung reactions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IgE mediates the allergic response but does not crystallize into these structures.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Myeloperoxidase is a neutrophil granule enzyme and is not the constituent of these crystals.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Surfactant protein is produced by pneumocytes and is unrelated to Charcot-Leyden crystal formation.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman develops an intensely itchy, serpiginous rash on her buttocks after lying on sand where dogs frequently defecate. Over the next three weeks the rash migrates and then resolves on its own. She never develops cough or gastrointestinal symptoms, and repeated stool studies are negative. Which of the following best explains this course?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The eggs require embryonation in soil, so the stool remains negative

choices.label: B
choices.text: The larvae cannot enter human blood vessels and die within the skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: The larvae reached the lungs but were cleared without causing symptoms

choices.label: D
choices.text: The larvae were killed by an IgE response before penetrating the skin

choices.label: E
choices.text: The worms matured in the colon and were expelled before laying eggs

explanation.summary: Ancylostoma braziliense is a dog hookworm whose larvae cannot enter human blood vessels, so infection stays confined to skin.
explanation.whyCorrect: A. braziliense is passed in the stool of dogs, and its larvae penetrate the skin of people who walk or lie on contaminated soil and sand. Unlike the other Ancylostoma and Necator species, it cannot get into human blood vessels. It is therefore doomed to crawl under the skin for days to weeks before dying, producing an itchy, pruritic, often serpiginous rash with no lung or gastrointestinal symptoms and no eggs in stool.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Stool is negative because no adults ever established in her gut, not because of an embryonation delay.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Failure to reach the circulation is the point; the larvae never make it to the lungs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The larvae clearly did penetrate the skin, which is what produced the migrating track.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The worms never reach the intestine at all in this infection, so colonic maturation does not occur.

questions.stem: A stool specimen from a patient with a suspected soil-transmitted helminth infection is examined by light microscopy. Which of the following egg descriptions is most consistent with Ancylostoma/Necator spp.?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A smooth-shelled oval egg whose interior contains multiple nodules

choices.label: B
choices.text: A thick-walled egg with radial striations and a six-hooked embryo inside

choices.label: C
choices.text: A transparent, elongated egg that is noticeably flattened along one side

choices.label: D
choices.text: An egg covered in rounded, bumpy protrusions across its outer surface

choices.label: E
choices.text: An operculated egg bearing a small knob at the end opposite the lid

explanation.summary: Hookworm eggs have a smooth outer shell with multiple internal nodules that represent the developing embryo.
explanation.whyCorrect: Identifying eggs in stool is the most common way hookworm infections are diagnosed. The eggs of Ancylostoma/Necator spp. have a smooth outer shell, and the interior shows multiple nodules, which are the embryo. Distinguishing the individual species requires further testing beyond routine microscopy.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Radially striated eggs containing a hexacanth embryo belong to tapeworms, not hookworms.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Transparent elongated eggs flattened on one side are those of Enterobius vermicularis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bumpy, mammillated surfaces characterize the unfertilized eggs of Ascaris spp.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Operculated eggs with a terminal knob are not the morphology described for hookworms.

questions.stem: A physician counsels a family relocating to a region where Strongyloides spp. and Ancylostoma/Necator spp. are endemic. Which of the following is the most effective measure to prevent infection with these particular parasites?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Boiling or filtering all drinking water before consuming it

choices.label: B
choices.text: Thoroughly cooking all freshwater fish before eating it

choices.label: C
choices.text: Thoroughly cooking all pork and beef before eating it

choices.label: D
choices.text: Washing hands carefully with soap before every meal

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wearing shoes and avoiding skin contact with the soil

explanation.summary: Skin-penetrating worms are prevented by wearing shoes and avoiding skin contact with contaminated soil.
explanation.whyCorrect: Strongyloides spp. and Ancylostoma/Necator spp. both begin infection when filariform larvae in soil burrow through intact skin. Because there is no ingestion step, food and water precautions do not help; the barrier that matters is physical separation of skin from soil. Wearing shoes and avoiding skin contact with soil in endemic areas is the preventive measure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Water treatment addresses fecal-orally transmitted organisms such as Ascaris, not skin penetration.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cooking freshwater fish prevents a fish tapeworm infection, which is a different transmission route.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cooking meat destroys cysts in tissue and prevents tapeworm infections, not skin-penetrating nematodes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Handwashing prevents fecal-oral spread of Ascaris and pinworm but not larval skin penetration.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy living in a community with poor sanitation passes a 25-cm-long worm in his stool. Which of the following is the most likely route by which he acquired this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Contact with the saliva of an infected household dog or cat

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ingestion of embryonated eggs in contaminated food or water

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ingestion of undercooked beef containing encysted larval cysts

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhalation of eggs aerosolized from dried contaminated topsoil

choices.label: E
choices.text: Penetration of intact skin by filariform larvae present in soil

explanation.summary: Ascaris, the giant roundworm, is transmitted fecal-orally by ingesting embryonated eggs.
explanation.whyCorrect: A worm of this size is Ascaris, whose adults range from 15 to 35 cm. Unlike Strongyloides and the hookworms, Ascaris spp. cannot burrow directly into skin. They are transmitted fecal-orally, usually through consumption of contaminated food or water, and it is specifically the ingestion of embryonated eggs that begins the infection. Areas where human feces contaminate water and soil carry the highest burden.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Contact with animal saliva plays no role in the fecal-oral transmission of Ascaris.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Larvae encysted in undercooked beef transmit tapeworms, which are cestodes rather than roundworms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ascaris eggs are not transmitted by inhalation; they must be swallowed.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Skin penetration by filariform larvae is the route for Strongyloides and hookworms, not Ascaris.

questions.stem: Which of the following helminth infections is the most common worldwide, affecting an estimated 800 million to 1.2 billion people?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ascariasis caused by Ascaris lumbricoides

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cutaneous larva migrans from Ancylostoma braziliense

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enterobiasis caused by Enterobius vermicularis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hookworm infection caused by Necator americanus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Strongyloidiasis caused by Strongyloides stercoralis

explanation.summary: Ascariasis is the most common helminth infection globally, with an estimated 800 million to 1.2 billion cases.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ascaris spp., the giant roundworms, cause the most common helminth infection in the world, with around 800 million to 1.2 billion people infected. A. lumbricoides causes most human cases, though A. suum from pigs can also infect people. The parasite is most common in tropical regions with poor sanitation, and Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America, and Southeast Asia carry the highest burden.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cutaneous larva migrans from the dog hookworm is a self-limited skin condition, not the leading global helminthiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pinworm is very common, especially in children, but is not the figure cited here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hookworm infections affect over 700 million people, still below the ascariasis figure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Strongyloidiasis affects an estimated 613 million people, fewer than ascariasis.

questions.stem: A child with ascariasis has a bowel movement in the yard of a home with poor sanitation. Another child playing in that same yard a few hours later ingests some of the contaminated soil. Which of the following best predicts the outcome?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Infection is unlikely, because Ascaris eggs are rapidly destroyed by stomach acid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Infection is unlikely, because the eggs must embryonate for weeks to be infectious

choices.label: C
choices.text: Infection occurs, because Ascaris eggs are infectious the moment they are passed

choices.label: D
choices.text: Infection occurs, because filariform larvae in the stool penetrate the gut wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Infection occurs, because the eggs hatch within minutes of leaving the host

explanation.summary: Freshly passed Ascaris eggs are not infectious; they must embryonate in the environment for roughly 18 days or longer.
explanation.whyCorrect: Once Ascaris eggs are passed in stool, they require about 18 days to several weeks in the environment to embryonate and become infectious. Eating unembryonated eggs does not transmit the infection. This lag is why fresh fecal contamination is less immediately dangerous than long-standing soil contamination, and it also distinguishes ascariasis from pinworm, whose eggs become infective within hours.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gastric acid is not the barrier; the limiting factor is the maturation state of the egg.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Eggs are not infectious at the moment of passage; the embryonation period is required first.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ascaris cannot penetrate skin or gut wall as a free larva; infection begins with a swallowed embryonated egg.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ascaris eggs do not hatch in the environment; they hatch after an embryonated egg is swallowed.

questions.stem: A 5-year-old child in a rural tropical village presents with vomiting, severe abdominal pain, and distention. Imaging shows a small bowel obstruction with a tubular intraluminal mass. During the evaluation, a long worm emerges from the child's nose. Which of the following organisms is most likely responsible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ancylostoma braziliense, which never reaches the human gut

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ascaris lumbricoides, whose adults are 15 to 35 cm long

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enterobius vermicularis, whose adults are 2 to 13 mm long

choices.label: D
choices.text: Necator americanus, whose adults are about 1 cm long

choices.label: E
choices.text: Strongyloides stercoralis, whose adults are 1 to 6 mm long

explanation.summary: Only Ascaris is large and numerous enough to obstruct bowel and to emerge from the mouth or nose.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most ascariasis is asymptomatic, but a high disease burden causes severe problems because of the sheer size and number of the worms. Intestinal obstruction, abdominal pain, and perforation with hemorrhage can occur, and heavy burdens can occlude ductal structures. In rare instances an adult female migrates up and emerges from the patient's mouth or nose, which is essentially pathognomonic given the worm's 15 to 35 cm length.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A. braziliense larvae die in the skin and never reach the intestine in humans.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pinworms are only millimeters long and live in the colon; they cannot obstruct bowel.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hookworm adults are roughly 1 cm and attach to the intestinal lining without forming a mass.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Strongyloides adults are 1 to 6 mm and are embedded in mucosa, far too small to obstruct.

questions.stem: Light microscopy of a stool specimen reveals an elongated oval egg with a thick outer coat bearing prominent, irregular rounded protrusions over its entire surface. Which of the following is the best interpretation of this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A fertilized Ascaris egg, which is round and relatively smooth

choices.label: B
choices.text: A hookworm egg, whose shell is smooth with internal nodules

choices.label: C
choices.text: A pinworm egg, which is transparent and flat along one side

choices.label: D
choices.text: A Strongyloides egg, rarely seen since larvae hatch in the gut

choices.label: E
choices.text: An unfertilized Ascaris egg, known as a mammillated egg

explanation.summary: Unfertilized Ascaris eggs are elongated and covered in rounded bumps, and are called mammillated eggs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Microscopic visualization of eggs is the most common way ascariasis is diagnosed. Unfertilized eggs are covered with rounded bumps and are described as mammillated. Fertilized eggs are rounder and still carry bumps but are overall smoother in appearance. Both forms can be found in the stool of infected patients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A fertilized Ascaris egg is rounder and overall smoother, not prominently and irregularly bumpy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hookworm eggs have a smooth outer shell with nodules inside, not bumps on the surface.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pinworm eggs are transparent, elongated, and slightly flattened on one side, without surface protrusions.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Strongyloides eggs hatch within the intestinal mucosa, so larvae rather than eggs appear in stool.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old girl has several weeks of intense perianal itching that is worst at night and disturbs her sleep. Her 5-year-old brother has similar symptoms. Which of the following best explains the nocturnal timing of her symptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adult worms burrow into the perianal skin during periods of rest

choices.label: B
choices.text: Eggs on the perianal skin are able to hatch only in the dark

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gravid female worms migrate to the anus at night to lay their eggs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Histamine release from cutaneous mast cells peaks during the night

choices.label: E
choices.text: Larvae migrate through the lungs at night, causing referred itching

explanation.summary: Pinworm itching is nocturnal because gravid females migrate to the anus at night to deposit eggs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Enterobius vermicularis adults mature and reproduce in the colon, and the gravid females then migrate to the anus at night to lay eggs. The eggs are coated in a sticky, irritating mucus-like substance that causes inflammation and intense itching around the anus and perianal region, especially at night. Pinworm spreads readily within households, which is why the sibling is affected too.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The adults remain in the bowel lumen; they lay eggs on the skin rather than burrowing into it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Egg maturation depends on time, not darkness, and occurs within a few hours.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The itching is driven by the irritating egg coating deposited at night, not by a circadian mast cell rhythm.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pinworms have no pulmonary migration phase in their life cycle.

questions.stem: A pediatrician wants to confirm a diagnosis of enterobiasis in a 7-year-old with nocturnal perianal itching. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnostic approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A single stool ova and parasite examination collected in the afternoon

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cellulose tape applied to the perianal skin after an evening shower

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cellulose tape applied to the perianal skin in the morning before bathing

choices.label: D
choices.text: Duodenal aspiration performed under conscious sedation in the clinic

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serologic testing for anti-Enterobius immunoglobulin G antibodies

explanation.summary: Pinworm is diagnosed with a cellulose tape sample from the perianal skin taken in the morning before bathing or defecation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because the gravid females deposit eggs on the perianal skin rather than in the bowel lumen, the best way to identify pinworms is to use cellulose tape on the perianal region and examine it microscopically. The sample should ideally be collected in the morning before bathing and before defecation, so that the eggs have not been washed or wiped away prior to collection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Eggs are laid on perianal skin rather than passed in feces, so routine stool studies are a poor test.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Sampling after a shower washes the eggs away, defeating the purpose of the tape test.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Duodenal aspiration samples the small intestine and is used for strongyloidiasis, not for pinworm.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serology is not the described method for identifying Enterobius vermicularis.

questions.stem: An outbreak of enterobiasis is being investigated at a residential facility. Which of the following best characterizes the populations affected and the transmission features of this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adults over 65 in tropical regions; spread by contact with contaminated soil

choices.label: B
choices.text: Agricultural workers in equatorial climates; larvae penetrate the skin of the feet

choices.label: C
choices.text: Children under 10 and crowded households; eggs survive on towels and clothing

choices.label: D
choices.text: Immunosuppressed adults worldwide; spread by autoinfection within the lungs

choices.label: E
choices.text: Travelers returning from Southeast Asia; spread by eating undercooked fish

explanation.summary: Pinworm occurs worldwide and primarily affects children under 10, household members, and people in crowded or institutional settings.
explanation.whyCorrect: Enterobius vermicularis occurs worldwide and primarily affects children under 10, people in crowded areas, household members of an infected person, and institutional populations. In addition to direct fecal-oral spread, the eggs can survive on towels, clothing, and other surfaces and transmit infection that way, which is why outbreaks in residential facilities are common.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pinworm is not soil-transmitted and does not preferentially affect older adults in the tropics.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Skin penetration by larvae in soil describes Strongyloides and hookworm, not pinworm.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Autoinfection involving the lungs describes Strongyloides hyperinfection, not enterobiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Undercooked fish transmits a tapeworm, and pinworm is not a travel-associated infection.

questions.stem: Microscopic examination of material collected on cellulose tape from a child's perianal skin reveals numerous parasite eggs. Which of the following descriptions best fits these eggs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Operculated eggs with a prominent knob at the opposite pole

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oval eggs with a smooth shell and a nodular embryo inside

choices.label: C
choices.text: Round eggs with a thick, bumpy, mammillated outer coat

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thick-shelled eggs with radial striations and six hooklets

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transparent, elongated eggs that are slightly flat on one side

explanation.summary: Enterobius vermicularis eggs are transparent, elongated, and slightly flattened along one side.
explanation.whyCorrect: The eggs recovered on cellulose tape from the perianal region are those of E. vermicularis, which are transparent, elongated, and slightly flat on one side. That asymmetric ovoid profile is what allows them to be distinguished from the eggs of the other intestinal nematodes. Larvae inside these eggs mature within only 4 to 6 hours, which is why self-reinfection by scratching is so efficient.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Operculated eggs with a terminal knob do not match the pinworm morphology described.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Smooth-shelled eggs with internal nodules are those of Ancylostoma/Necator spp.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bumpy mammillated eggs are the unfertilized eggs of Ascaris spp.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Radially striated eggs containing a six-hooked embryo are tapeworm eggs.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy is treated for pinworm infection but becomes symptomatic again several weeks later despite no new household or school contacts. Which of the following pairs of facts best explains where the adult worms reside and why he relapsed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adults live in the colon and cecum; relapse follows eggs carried on the fingers

choices.label: B
choices.text: Adults live in the duodenal submucosa; relapse follows asexual egg production

choices.label: C
choices.text: Adults live in the gallbladder; relapse follows eggs shed into the biliary tree

choices.label: D
choices.text: Adults live in the jejunum; relapse follows dormant tissue larvae reactivating

choices.label: E
choices.text: Adults live in the lung parenchyma; relapse follows larvae being coughed up

explanation.summary: Pinworm adults reproduce in the colon and cecum, and scratching transfers eggs to the fingers, which are then reingested.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ingested pinworm eggs hatch in the small intestine, and the worms mature and migrate to the colon, where they reproduce; the adults are found in the lumen of the cecum. When patients scratch the itchy perianal skin, trace amounts of feces and eggs end up on their fingers, which can be spread in the environment or swallowed. Eggs consumed this way hatch and restart the cycle, so patients repeatedly reinfect themselves and infection can persist long past the roughly 2-month lifespan of an individual adult.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Submucosal females producing eggs asexually describe Strongyloides stercoralis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pinworms do not inhabit the gallbladder or shed eggs into the biliary tree.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Jejunal adults and dormant reactivating tissue larvae describe hookworm biology, not pinworm.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pinworms have no pulmonary stage; no larvae are coughed up in this infection.
